Deputy Governor **Poonam Gupta** raised the possibility of a hike later this year; external members **Ram Singh and Saugata Bhattacharya** also flagged the need for swift policy recalibration.
The benchmark **10-year government bond yield jumped as much as 4 basis points to 6.86%**, and 5-year yields rose **8 bps to 6.53%**, as traders repriced the outlook.
**Goldman Sachs** now expects quarter-point hikes in **December and February**; a Nomura economist said the hawkish tone challenged her own call for an extended pause.

depth.background: The **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** held its policy rate — the **repo rate** — unchanged at **5.25%** at its August meeting earlier this month, with a 'neutral' stance that markets read as leaving room to cut later if needed. But the RBI also publishes detailed **minutes** of its rate-setting committee's internal discussion a couple of weeks after the decision — and those minutes often move markets more than the headline decision itself, because they reveal how divided or convinced the committee actually was.

cards.title: ED raids revive an 8-year-old ₹113-crore crypto scam, traces alleged kingpin to Dubai
cards.what_happened: The ED's Mumbai Zonal Office carried out search operations across multiple properties in Mumbai and Thane connected to the MTC cryptocurrency investment scheme, seizing roughly ₹1 crore in cash along with incriminating documents and digital devices. Investigators allege investors were cheated of about ₹113 crore after the scheme's operators manipulated the value of the MTC coin across several linked platforms to attract and retain buyers. The agency named Amit Madanlal Lakhanpal as the alleged mastermind; he and some associates are accused of leaving India after obtaining Antigua and Barbuda passports through a citizenship-by-investment program and are now believed to be living in Dubai under assumed identities. The ED also summoned Taha Hafiz Qazi, described as technical support staff, and chief accountant Sachin Vasant Shelar for questioning. The agency is expected to seek Interpol's help if it confirms Lakhanpal remains in Dubai.
key_points: India's **Enforcement Directorate** searched properties in **Mumbai and Thane** tied to the **MTC (Money Trade Coin)** cryptocurrency scheme, seizing about **₹1 crore in cash**.
Investors were allegedly cheated of around **₹113 crore** through a scheme that manipulated the value of its own coin to lure and retain buyers.
The alleged mastermind, **Amit Madanlal Lakhanpal**, is accused of fleeing to **Dubai** on an **Antigua and Barbuda passport** obtained through a citizenship-by-investment scheme.
The case had **languished for nearly a decade** in local Thane police files before this ED action — its first serious central-agency move.

depth.background: India's Enforcement Directorate (ED) is the federal agency that investigates financial crimes like money laundering, and it often steps into cases that started as local police complaints once cross-border money trails emerge. The MTC scheme is an old one: it dates back roughly eight years, when it promised investors returns from a cryptocurrency called Money Trade Coin. Complaints piled up with Thane City Police, but the case saw little central-agency movement for years — a common pattern in India's early-generation crypto fraud cases, many of which pre-date the country's current crypto regulations.

cards.title: Sensex and Nifty snap a six-day winning streak as investors turn cautious ahead of Powell's Jackson Hole speech
cards.what_happened: Indian benchmark indices closed lower on **Friday, August 22**, ending a six-day winning streak. The **Sensex** settled at 81,306.85, down 693.86 points or 0.85%, while the **Nifty 50** fell 213.65 points, also 0.85%, to close at 24,870.10. The decline was broad-based: 25 of the Sensex's 30 constituent stocks fell, including heavyweights like **HDFC Bank, TCS, ICICI Bank, Asian Paints and Tech Mahindra**, down as much as 2%. Sector-wise, metals, PSU banks and private banks led the losses, falling over 1% each. The pullback followed a sharp rally earlier in the week driven by GST-reform optimism, but for the week as a whole the indices still ended around 1% higher.
key_points: Sensex fell **693.86 points (0.85%)** to close at 81,306.85; Nifty 50 dropped **213.65 points (0.85%)** to 24,870.10.
The fall **snapped a six-session rally** that had been fuelled by optimism over India's GST reforms.
Selling was broad-based, with **25 of 30 Sensex stocks** trading lower, including HDFC Bank, TCS and ICICI Bank.
Investors turned cautious ahead of Fed Chair **Jerome Powell's Jackson Hole speech** later Friday, which markets watch for interest-rate hints.
Despite Friday's drop, both indices still ended the **week roughly 1% higher**.

depth.background: Indian markets had been on a strong run this week, lifted by optimism that the government's push to simplify **GST (Goods and Services Tax)** into just two slabs would boost consumption, plus hopes of a possible **credit-rating upgrade** from S&P. That rally ran into a wall of caution as traders positioned ahead of the **Jackson Hole Symposium** — an annual gathering of central bankers in Wyoming, US — where the Federal Reserve chair's speech is scrutinised for clues on the future path of US interest rates. Since global bond yields and Fed policy directly influence how much foreign money flows into or out of emerging markets like India, uncertainty ahead of that speech is enough to trigger profit-taking.

cards.title: Justice Sanjay Karol retires from the Supreme Court after a term marked by access-to-justice rulings
cards.what_happened: Justice Sanjay Karol formally retired from the Supreme Court of India on **August 22, 2026**, closing out a three-and-a-half-year tenure on the top court. The **Supreme Court Bar Association** and the **Supreme Court Advocates-on-Record Association** each held farewell functions in his honour. Chief Justice Surya Kant praised his commitment to 'accessibility and institutional dignity,' noting the bench loses 'an officer who combined administrative reform with a human approach to litigation.' Over his career, Justice Karol authored more than 270 judgements, including a landmark Patna High Court ruling that recognised access to clean public toilets as a **fundamental right**, and he is credited with more than halving pending cases during his time as Tripura's Chief Justice.
key_points: Justice Sanjay Karol demitted office from the **Supreme Court of India on August 22**, after a **three-and-a-half-year tenure**.
He authored **over 270 judgements**, including a Patna High Court ruling recognising **access to clean toilets as a fundamental right**.
As Chief Justice of Tripura, he helped **cut case pendency by more than half**.
Chief Justice **Surya Kant** praised him as 'a judge who lived the Constitution' at his farewell.
He is one of **five Supreme Court judges retiring in 2026**, part of a broader generational turnover on the bench.

depth.background: India's Supreme Court judges retire mandatorily at **age 65**, and 2026 is a year with an unusually large number of retirements reshaping the court's composition. Justice Karol rose through the Himachal Pradesh High Court before serving as **Chief Justice of Tripura and Patna High Courts**, then was elevated to the Supreme Court, where he built a reputation for rulings that connected constitutional principles to everyday, practical access-to-justice issues rather than only high-profile political cases.

cards.title: India and Singapore hold 4th Ministerial Roundtable, deepening trade and tech ties
cards.what_happened: India's top economic and foreign-policy ministers — **Sitharaman, Jaishankar and Goyal** — travelled to Singapore for a three-day visit culminating in the **4th ISMR** on August 20, meeting Singapore's Deputy PM **Gan Kim Yong** and other senior ministers. The two sides discussed strengthening their **Comprehensive Strategic Partnership**, with a specific focus on advanced manufacturing, digital cooperation, sustainability, and physical/digital connectivity. Alongside the ministerial talks, a **Business Roundtable** convened companies from both countries to explore new investment and Global Capability Centre opportunities.
key_points: Union Ministers **Nirmala Sitharaman (Finance)**, **S. Jaishankar (External Affairs)** and **Piyush Goyal (Commerce)** led India's delegation to the **4th India-Singapore Ministerial Roundtable** in Singapore.
Singapore's side was led by **Deputy PM Gan Kim Yong**, alongside ministers covering security, foreign affairs, digital policy and finance.
Talks focused on deepening the countries' **Comprehensive Strategic Partnership** — spanning **advanced manufacturing, digitalisation, sustainability and connectivity**.
A parallel **4th India-Singapore Business Roundtable** brought companies together to explore investment and **Global Capability Centre** opportunities.
Singapore is already one of India's **largest sources of foreign investment**; the roundtable aims to convert this dialogue into concrete deals.

depth.background: The **India-Singapore Ministerial Roundtable (ISMR)** is a periodic high-level dialogue format — this was its fourth edition — meant to fast-track cooperation between the two countries beyond routine diplomacy. Singapore has long served as a **financial and logistics gateway** connecting India to Southeast Asia and global capital markets, and hosts many multinational firms' regional headquarters and India-facing back offices known as **Global Capability Centres (GCCs)**.

cards.title: Amit Shah chairs Southern Zonal Council as states press him on delimitation and water-sharing
cards.what_happened: Home Minister **Amit Shah** chaired the 31st Southern Zonal Council meeting on **August 20, 2026**, in Tamil Nadu, bringing together chief ministers and senior ministers from the five southern states. The agenda centred on **inter-state river water disputes**, demands for greater **central tax devolution** (the share of nationally collected taxes states receive back), and simmering anxiety over the coming **delimitation** exercise. Shah used the platform to praise the region's economic contribution — from **IT and AI to space, pharmaceuticals and automobiles** — while state leaders pushed back on issues they say the Centre has been slow to resolve.
key_points: Union Home Minister **Amit Shah** chaired the **31st Southern Zonal Council** meeting on **August 20** in Kovalam/Mahabalipuram, Tamil Nadu.
Chief Ministers and senior leaders from **Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka and Kerala** attended, alongside Telangana's representation.
Southern leaders pressed for faster resolution of **inter-state river water-sharing disputes** and a fairer share of **central tax devolution**.
States also raised concerns about the upcoming **delimitation** exercise — the redrawing of Lok Sabha seats — fearing it could **cut the South's political weight** for controlling population growth.
Shah highlighted the South's outsized contribution to **IT, AI, space, pharma, and agriculture**, calling it a major national growth engine.

depth.background: **Zonal Councils** are statutory forums (five across India, grouping neighbouring states) created to let states thrash out inter-state disputes — water, boundaries, taxes — with the Union government as mediator, chaired on rotation by the Union Home Minister. The Southern Zonal Council covers **Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, Kerala, Telangana** and nearby Union Territories. Delimitation and water-sharing are long-running sore points for the South: southern states industrialised earlier and controlled population growth more successfully than many northern states, which they fear will now be used against them if parliamentary seats are reallocated purely by current population.

cards.title: Rahul Gandhi sits on a police-station dharna over a pellet-gun victim — and Delhi Police agrees to file an FIR
cards.what_happened: On Thursday, Rahul Gandhi visited two Delhi police stations with Sahil Lochab, demanding an FIR be registered over the pellet-gun injuries Lochab suffered on July 20. After a meeting with Deputy Commissioner of Police (Central) Sachin Sharma failed to produce a commitment, Gandhi and Lochab sat down in a dharna (sit-in protest) outside the Parliament Street police station. Police told them the refusal to register an FIR came on **'orders from the top,'** implying political pressure from above. Priyanka Gandhi, Salman Khurshid, Randeep Singh Surjewala, and other senior Congress figures joined the protest. Union Minister **JP Nadda** criticized the demonstration as **'cheap, attention-seeking politics.'** Following the standoff, Delhi Police agreed to register the FIR.
key_points: Gandhi protested with **Sahil Lochab**, a 19-year-old allegedly hit by police pellets during a **July 20 Jantar Mantar student protest**.
An **AIIMS medical report** reportedly found over **200 shells lodged in his body**, including **3 in one eye**, costing him his vision there.
Police initially refused to register an FIR, telling Gandhi they had **'orders from the top.'**
Priyanka Gandhi and senior Congress leaders **joined the sit-in** after talks with a police officer failed.
Delhi Police later **agreed to register the FIR** after the standoff drew national attention.

depth.background: An FIR (First Information Report) is the formal document Indian police must file to officially open a criminal investigation — without one, a complaint effectively goes nowhere. Sahil Lochab was injured on July 20 during a student protest at Delhi's Jantar Mantar/Connaught Place, allegedly hit by pellets fired by police, and was treated first at Lady Hardinge Hospital before being referred to AIIMS, India's top public hospital. Rahul Gandhi, the Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha (India's lower house of Parliament), has repeatedly used direct, visible protests like this to pressure the government on issues of alleged state overreach.

cards.title: RBI's deputy governor says India's growth may beat forecasts and near 7%
cards.what_happened: Speaking at an event hosted by the Madras School of Economics in Chennai, RBI Deputy Governor Poonam Gupta said India's economic growth for the financial year ending March could come in close to **7%**, beating the central bank's official **6.7% forecast**. She attributed the upbeat outlook to an expected strong April–June quarter, with official growth figures for that quarter due to be released later this month. She added: **'Going forward, notwithstanding these shocks, I would say, 7.5 per cent is a given and we should aspire to do better than that.'** Her comments come even as she acknowledged the economy faces real headwinds, including an inadequate monsoon and elevated energy costs.
key_points: **Poonam Gupta**, RBI Deputy Governor, said growth could come in near **7%**, above the RBI's own **6.7% forecast**.
Her optimism rests on an expected **strong April–June quarter**, with official data due later this month.
Economists' estimates for the quarter range widely, from **6.9% to 8%**.
Gupta said India should ultimately **'aspire' to 7.5%-plus** annual growth over time.
This comes despite headwinds like a **patchy monsoon** and **elevated energy costs**.

depth.background: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) is India's central bank, and its Monetary Policy Committee sets interest rates partly based on how fast the economy is growing — faster growth with high inflation typically argues for holding or raising rates, while slower growth argues for cuts. GDP (Gross Domestic Product) growth is the broadest measure of how much an economy's output of goods and services expanded over a period, usually a year or a quarter. India has been one of the world's fastest-growing major economies, and the RBI's own forecasts are watched closely as a baseline that markets, businesses, and the government plan around.

cards.title: India orders telcos to strictly enforce the 9-SIM-per-person limit from August 24
cards.what_happened: The Department of Telecommunications has told telecom operators to **strictly enforce** the existing cap on SIM cards per customer — **9 nationally**, **6** in Jammu & Kashmir, Assam and the North-Eastern states — starting **August 24, 2026**. Under the new process, operators must check the DoT's centralized **Digital Intelligence Platform (DIP)**, which aggregates subscriber records from every operator, before issuing a new SIM to see whether an applicant has already hit their limit; from **August 23** the platform will also show a representative photo of the subscriber to help with identity verification. If a connection is activated beyond the limit — even for a single day — it must be **suspended immediately** until the issue is resolved. Operators have until **November 30** to fully align their internal systems with the DIP.
key_points: From **August 24**, telecom operators must actively check and block customers trying to exceed India's legal SIM-card limit.
The limit has stood since **2012**: a maximum of **9 mobile connections per person** nationwide, and **6** in Jammu & Kashmir, Assam and the North-East.
Operators must use the government's **Digital Intelligence Platform (DIP)**, which pools subscriber data across every telecom company to spot repeat offenders.
From **August 23**, DIP will even surface a subscriber's photo to help operators verify identity before issuing a new SIM.
Any connection activated over the limit must be **suspended immediately** until resolved; full technical compliance is due by **November 30**.

depth.background: Indian law has capped how many mobile connections one person can hold since **2012**, largely as a fraud- and crime-prevention measure — SIM cards bought in bulk, often on fake or stolen identities, are a common tool for phone scams, OTP fraud and other cybercrime in India. Enforcement has historically been patchy because no single telecom operator could see how many SIMs a customer already held with *rival* operators. The government's Department of Telecommunications has been building the Sanchar Saathi citizen platform and its underlying Digital Intelligence Platform specifically to close that gap by giving every operator a shared, real-time view across the whole industry.

cards.title: Delhi ramps up security and infrastructure prep for the BRICS Summit it hosts next month
cards.what_happened: Delhi's Lieutenant Governor, **Taranjit Singh Sandhu**, chaired a review meeting on **August 20** covering security, traffic management, civic infrastructure and emergency medical arrangements ahead of the **BRICS Summit 2026**, which India will host in Delhi on **September 12–13**. This is the **18th BRICS Summit**, held under India's chairship around the theme **'Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability.'** Sandhu directed key departments and civic bodies to tighten security protocols, streamline traffic across the city, maintain infrastructure, and deploy comprehensive emergency medical readiness across summit venues and the transit corridors leaders' motorcades will use. He stressed that all agencies must work in 'multi-agency coordination' and finish their assigned tasks on time, with preparations to continue without interruption until the summit.
key_points: Delhi's Lieutenant Governor **Taranjit Singh Sandhu** chaired a review of security, traffic and infrastructure readiness for the **BRICS Summit 2026**.
India hosts the **18th BRICS Summit** in Delhi on **September 12–13** — its first time chairing the bloc's annual leaders' summit.
The LG ordered every civic and security agency into **multi-agency coordination** covering venues and transit corridors.
India's chairship theme is **'Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability.'**
Preparations extend beyond security and traffic to **emergency medical readiness** ahead of world leaders' arrival.

depth.background: BRICS is a grouping of major emerging economies — originally **B**razil, **R**ussia, **I**ndia, **C**hina and **S**outh Africa — that has since added more members and positions itself as a voice for the 'Global South' alongside Western-led forums like the G7. The bloc holds an annual leaders' summit, with the host and chair rotating each year; hosting is a chance for that country to help set the agenda and showcase itself to visiting heads of state. India has run major global summits before — it hosted the G20 leaders' summit in Delhi in 2023 — and treats these events as high-stakes logistics operations given the security needs of dozens of foreign leaders converging on one city.

prev_ref.title: Sensex and Nifty snap a seven-day losing streak as global bond jitters ease

cards.title: Sensex, Nifty end a volatile session almost flat as crude and bond-yield stress cap the rally
cards.what_happened: Indian markets opened higher on Friday, extending Thursday's bounce, with the Sensex briefly up over 160 points and the Nifty near 24,300. But the gains evaporated through the day, and both indices closed almost exactly where they started: the **Sensex finished up just 3.11 points at 77,540.83**, and the **Nifty rose 20.15 points to 24,252.00** — both essentially flat. Sector performance was split: metal, realty and select pharma names attracted buying, while IT, FMCG, auto and media stocks weighed the index down. The muted session came as **Brent crude neared $94 a barrel** and global bond yields kept climbing, both of which make investors more cautious about holding riskier equities.
key_points: Sensex closed up just **3.11 points at 77,540.83**; Nifty rose **20.15 points to 24,252.00** — essentially unchanged.
The session was **rangebound and volatile**, giving back most of the morning's opening gains.
**Brent crude oil** approaching **$94 a barrel** and rising US bond yields kept investors cautious.
**Metal and realty stocks** gained while **IT, FMCG, auto, media and pharma** shares dragged the index down.
It follows Thursday's rally that snapped a **seven-session losing streak** — today's flat close shows that bounce has stalled.

thread.previously: We reported that the Sensex and Nifty snapped a seven-session losing streak on Thursday as global bond-market jitters eased, with the Nifty up 0.64% and Sensex up 0.82%.
thread.changed: Friday's follow-through fizzled: both indices closed almost exactly flat as Brent crude neared $94 and bond yields kept climbing, showing the rebound hasn't yet turned into a sustained recovery.

depth.background: Indian equity benchmarks had been sliding for seven straight sessions before Thursday's rebound, hit by a mix of global bond-market stress, elevated crude oil prices, and Middle East tensions tied to the US-Iran standoff. Thursday's rally — Nifty up 0.64%, Sensex up 0.82% — offered relief, but analysts had already flagged that follow-through buying looked fragile given how many global headwinds remained unresolved. Global bond yields have been climbing worldwide this week, which makes borrowing more expensive everywhere and tends to pull money out of riskier assets like emerging-market stocks including India's.

cards.title: India and Japan sign a maritime security pact as defence ministers meet in New Delhi
cards.what_happened: Rajnath Singh hosted Japanese Defence Minister Shinjiro Koizumi in New Delhi for a bilateral meeting focused on strengthening defence cooperation and promoting stability in the Indo-Pacific. The two ministers signed a **Memorandum of Arrangement on Maritime Security Cooperation**, formalizing plans to deepen operational cooperation on maritime security in a 'practical and effective manner.' Ahead of the formal talks, Koizumi laid a wreath at the Gaurav Stambh war memorial, visited the Indian Navy's indigenous stealth destroyer **INS Chennai**, and held discussions with Indian Navy Chief Admiral Krishna Swaminathan and the Western Naval Command. Koizumi said afterward he would 'devote all my efforts to turn discussions into outcomes.'
key_points: Defence Minister **Rajnath Singh** and Japan's **Shinjiro Koizumi** met in New Delhi to deepen defence ties.
The two sides signed a **Memorandum of Arrangement on Maritime Security Cooperation**.
Both ministers committed to deeper cooperation for a **'free and open Indo-Pacific'**.
Talks also covered closer **defence equipment and technology collaboration** under the 'Make in India' push.
Koizumi visited the **indigenous warship INS Chennai** and met India's Navy chief before the formal meeting.

depth.background: India and Japan have steadily deepened defence and security ties over the past decade, largely as a hedge against China's growing assertiveness in the Indo-Pacific region — the vast maritime zone stretching from the eastern coast of Africa through the Indian Ocean to the Pacific. Both countries are part of the informal 'Quad' grouping with the US and Australia, built around similar concerns about freedom of navigation and security in these waters. Regular defence-minister meetings like this one are how the two governments turn broad strategic alignment into concrete agreements — from maritime patrols to shared equipment standards.

cards.title: India's home World Championships end in heartbreak as PV Sindhu and Lakshya Sen both crash out
cards.what_happened: PV Sindhu's campaign ended on Thursday when she lost a tight three-game round-of-16 match to China's third seed Wang Zhi Yi, 21-11, 15-21, 21-17, after having opened with straight-game wins over lower-ranked opponents. Lakshya Sen was eliminated even earlier, in the second round, losing 21-19, 19-21, 17-21 to the USA's unseeded Garret Tan — a result being described as one of the tournament's biggest upsets. The two losses mean India's singles medal hopes at its own World Championships are over before the semifinal stage, a disappointing outcome given the home-crowd advantage and India's rising profile in the sport. India's other hopes now rest on the doubles pair of Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty and rising singles player Ayush Shetty, both of whom are still through to the pre-quarterfinals.
key_points: Badminton's **BWF World Championships** are being held in New Delhi — India's **first time hosting since 2009**.
**PV Sindhu**, a two-time Olympic medallist chasing a record **6th World Championship medal**, lost her round-of-16 match **21-11, 15-21, 21-17** to China's Wang Zhi Yi.
**Lakshya Sen**, a 2021 bronze medallist, suffered a shock **second-round exit** to unseeded American Garret Tan.
Both losses end India's singles medal hopes at a tournament being played in front of a home crowd for the first time in 17 years.
Doubles pair **Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty**, and young singles player **Ayush Shetty**, remain alive in the draw.

depth.background: The World Championships are badminton's most prestigious event outside the Olympics, held annually and rotated among cities that bid to host it. India last hosted the tournament in **2009** in Hyderabad, so this New Delhi edition — running August 17–23 at the Indira Gandhi Arena — is a rare chance for Indian players to compete for a world title in front of a home crowd. Sindhu, now 31, has won more World Championship medals (five) than any other woman in the sport's history and came in hoping to add a sixth. Sen made his name with a bronze at the delayed 2021 edition and has been tipped as India's best men's singles hope since.

cards.title: Hyderabad hit-and-run: Jana Sena MP's son booked after his Aston Martin kills a 26-year-old woman
cards.what_happened: On August 16, **Bharathi Mukhi**, a 26-year-old employee at a Lifestyle store in Hyderabad's Inorbit Mall, was crossing the road in the Madhapur area when she was allegedly hit by a speeding **Aston Martin**. She suffered severe head injuries and was rushed to Apollo Hospital in Jubilee Hills, where doctors declared her dead on arrival. Police identified the driver as **Sanjush**, the son of Jana Sena's Rajya Sabha MP Lingamaneni Ramesh, and took him into custody the same day, administering drunk-driving and drug tests and sending blood samples for forensic analysis. He has now been booked under **Section 106(1) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita** (India's newer criminal code, which replaced the colonial-era IPC in 2024), the provision covering death caused by negligence.
key_points: **Bharathi Mukhi (26)**, a Lifestyle store employee, was struck and killed while crossing the road in Hyderabad's **Madhapur** area on August 16.
The Aston Martin was allegedly driven at high speed by **Sanjush**, the son of **Jana Sena Party Rajya Sabha MP Lingamaneni Ramesh**.
He was taken into custody the same day and given **drunk-driving and drug tests**; blood samples went to the Forensic Science Laboratory.
He has now been formally **booked under BNS Section 106(1)** — causing death by negligence.
The case has fed a recurring public debate in India about **luxury cars, speed, and impunity for the politically connected**.

depth.background: Hit-and-run and rash-driving cases involving the children of politicians or the wealthy are a recurring flashpoint in Indian public debate, often reigniting arguments over whether the well-connected face real legal consequences. The **Jana Sena Party**, led by actor-turned-politician Pawan Kalyan, is a coalition partner in Andhra Pradesh's ruling alliance, and **Lingamaneni Ramesh** sits in the **Rajya Sabha** (India's upper house of Parliament) as one of its members.

cards.title: Modi says 1937 Vande Mataram edit 'sowed the seeds of Partition' — Congress says he's insulting Tagore
cards.what_happened: PM Narendra Modi said that 'important stanzas of Vande Mataram — its very soul — were removed' in 1937, and argued that this **'divisive mindset'** was part of what eventually 'sowed the seeds of Partition' — the 1947 split of British India into India and Pakistan. Congress hit back by pointing to the actual **CWC resolution of October 28, 1937**, which recommended only the first two stanzas for official use, a call made on Tagore's advice and endorsed by a cross-section of Congress leadership including Jawaharlal Nehru, Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, Subhas Chandra Bose, Maulana Abul Kalam Azad, Govind Vallabh Pant, and Acharya Narendra Dev. Congress said Modi's framing effectively insults Tagore, who proposed the edit. Home Minister Amit Shah accused Congress of 'appeasement' politics that he said fed the two-nation theory — the ideological basis for Pakistan's creation — and BJP's Jairam Ramesh countered that the BJP's nationalism is 'fake.' The clash comes shortly after Parliament passed a law granting Vande Mataram the same statutory protection as the National Anthem, and after all six stanzas were sung in the Lok Sabha for the first time as the Monsoon Session closed on August 13.
key_points: PM Modi said the **stanzas dropped from Vande Mataram in 1937** removed its 'very soul' and reflected a **'divisive mindset'** that helped cause Partition.
Congress cites the actual **1937 Congress Working Committee (CWC) resolution**, drafted on **Rabindranath Tagore's advice**, as the source of the two-stanza tradition.
That 1937 decision was endorsed by **Nehru, Sardar Patel, Subhas Chandra Bose, Maulana Azad** and others — not one faction.
Home Minister **Amit Shah** called Congress's stance **'anti-national'**; Congress's Jairam Ramesh called BJP's nationalism **'fake.'**
The row follows Parliament's recent move giving Vande Mataram the **same statutory protection as the National Anthem**.

depth.background: 'Vande Mataram' ('I bow to thee, Mother') is a 19th-century poem by Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay that became a rallying song of India's independence movement, later adopted as the country's **National Song** (distinct from the National Anthem, 'Jana Gana Mana'). Only the poem's first two stanzas are commonly recited in official settings — a practice that traces back to a **1937 Congress Working Committee resolution**, taken on the advice of Nobel laureate **Rabindranath Tagore**, because the later stanzas invoke the Hindu goddess **Durga** in ways some felt could alienate non-Hindu Indians in a national song meant to unite everyone against British rule.

cards.title: Maharashtra bans sale of loose, unpacked cooking oil — violators face up to 7 years in jail
cards.what_happened: Maharashtra's FDA, led by Commissioner **Tukaram Mundhe**, has ordered a statewide ban on the sale of loose or unpacked edible oil, announced this week. Mundhe said the decision followed inspections that uncovered **adulteration, unauthorised blending, poor labelling, repackaging of old oil, and the use of unsuitable containers** at multiple outlets. Under the order, violators will be prosecuted under **Chapter IX of the Food Safety and Standards Act**, which allows for imprisonment and fines depending on the severity of the offence: unsafe food can draw jail time plus fines up to ₹10 lakh, substandard oil up to ₹5 lakh, misbranded oil up to ₹3 lakh, possession of adulterants up to ₹10 lakh, and operating without a valid licence up to ₹10 lakh. The FDA has warned it will take strict action against violators going forward.
key_points: Maharashtra's **Food and Drug Administration (FDA)** has banned the sale of **loose, unpacked edible oil** across the state
Violators face **imprisonment of up to 7 years** and fines running as high as **₹10 lakh** depending on the offence
FDA Commissioner **Tukaram Mundhe** said inspections found widespread **adulteration**, unauthorised blending, and repackaging of old oil in unsuitable containers
The crackdown will be enforced under **Chapter IX of the Food Safety and Standards Act**, which covers unsafe and substandard food
Separate penalty slabs apply for substandard oil, misbranded oil, possession of adulterants, and selling without a valid licence

depth.background: In much of India, cooking oil is still commonly sold **loose** — ladled out from large containers at local shops rather than sold pre-packaged and sealed — because it's often cheaper than branded, bottled oil. That informality, though, makes it far easier for sellers to **adulterate** oil (mix it with cheaper substances), reuse old or reheated oil, or store it in containers that aren't food-safe, all without a consumer being able to tell just by looking. India's **Food Safety and Standards Authority (FSSAI)** framework, enforced at the state level by bodies like Maharashtra's FDA, is meant to catch exactly this kind of unsafe practice, but enforcement against small, informal sellers has historically been patchy.

cards.title: Kolkata hotel fire that killed 9 Bangladeshi nationals: leaseholder arrested, owner still on the run
cards.what_happened: A fire tore through **Hotel Shikha Inn**, one of several hotels packed into a four-storey building on Kolkata's Mirza Ghalib Street, shortly after **2 am on August 19**. Nine people died, including a 4-year-old child, and several others were injured; all the victims confirmed dead so far are **Bangladeshi nationals** who were in Kolkata for medical treatment. Preliminary reports pointed to a possible **air-conditioner explosion** on an upper floor, though officials have not confirmed a cause. This week, Kolkata Police **arrested the hotel's leaseholder, Abu Zafar**, from Entally Main Market and detained two staff members for questioning, while the building's original owner, **Bireshwar Mitra, remains at large**. Police have set up a Special Investigation Team to determine whether the hotel was operating without adequate fire-safety clearances.
key_points: A pre-dawn fire at **Hotel Shikha Inn** on Kolkata's Mirza Ghalib Street killed **9 people**, including a 4-year-old child, all Bangladeshi nationals in the city for medical treatment
The blaze broke out around **2 am on August 19** in a four-storey building housing the hotel
Kolkata Police arrested the hotel's leaseholder, **Abu Zafar**, and detained **two staff members** for questioning
The hotel's original owner, **Bireshwar Mitra**, remains absconding as of this week
A **Special Investigation Team (SIT)** has been formed; the exact cause of the fire is still unconfirmed

depth.background: Kolkata's older, densely packed commercial districts — like the area around Mirza Ghalib Street — are lined with budget hotels that cater heavily to medical tourists from **Bangladesh**, who travel to Indian cities for treatment unavailable or unaffordable at home. Many of these buildings are decades old, converted from other uses, and fire-safety enforcement in India's crowded urban cores has long lagged behind the pace of construction — a gap that has produced a string of deadly hotel and building fires across Indian cities in recent years. A **leaseholder** runs the day-to-day hotel business, while the **owner** holds the underlying property, and both can face liability if the building itself was unsafe.

cards.title: Supreme Court cuts the mandatory law-practice rule for judge candidates from 3 years to 1, adds a year of training
cards.what_happened: The Supreme Court, in a verdict pronounced by **Chief Justice Surya Kant's bench** at **10:30 AM** on August 21, modified its own May 2025 ruling: instead of requiring 3 years of prior legal practice to sit the Civil Judge (Junior Division) exam, candidates now need just **1 year of practice**. The court added new requirements on the back end — successful candidates must complete **1 year of training at a judicial academy**, followed by **1 year of structured clerkship under a sitting judge**, before being confirmed as judicial officers, and will be paid half a magistrate's salary during that period. The court also carved out relief for graduates caught in limbo since its original ruling: anyone who graduated law school between **May 20, 2025 and March 31, 2027** can sit the exam with no prior practice requirement at all, but if selected, will be appointed only as a 'trainee judicial officer' and must still complete the training and clerkship. The bench separately heard a plea to relax the requirement for candidates with disabilities.
key_points: The court refused to scrap the practice requirement entirely but **cut it from 3 years to 1 year** of legal practice before candidates can sit the Civil Judge exam
Selected candidates must now also complete **1 year of judicial academy training** plus **1 year of supervised clerkship** before taking the bench
Trainees will be paid **half the salary** of a sitting Judicial Magistrate First Class during this training period
Law graduates from **May 2025 to March 2027** get a one-time waiver — they can sit the exam with **zero practice years**, but must still do the training and clerkship
The bench was led by **Chief Justice Surya Kant**, alongside Justices August George Masih and K Vinod Chandran

depth.background: In **May 2025**, the Supreme Court restored a rule requiring **3 years of legal practice** before law graduates could sit the entry-level exam to become a **Civil Judge (Junior Division)** — reversing years of letting fresh graduates apply directly. Petitioners, including bar associations and law students, argued the 3-year rule pushed talented graduates away from judicial careers by forcing years of often-unpaid junior lawyering first, at a time many state judiciaries face **judge shortages**. The court took the rare step of agreeing to review its own decision through review petitions, and today delivered its final word.

cards.title: Punjab shuts down for 7 hours as Sikh groups demand release of 'Bandi Singhs' who've finished their sentences
cards.what_happened: Allied groups under the **Qaumi Insaaf Morcha** banner called and enforced a **statewide bandh (shutdown)** across Punjab on August 21, running from **7 AM to 2 PM**, to press their demand for the release of Sikh prisoners the Morcha says have completed their sentences but remain incarcerated. Schools and colleges across the state stayed closed, shops and factories were asked to shut for the duration, and highways along with bus and other transport services were disrupted. The **SGPC**, the powerful body that manages Sikh religious institutions in Punjab, formally extended its support to the bandh call, lending it significant organizational weight. The call came after tensions escalated on **August 15**, when demonstrators tried to march toward Punjab Governor Gulab Chand Kataria's official residence in Chandigarh to press the same demand, and police used tear gas and water cannons to disperse the crowd after protesters tried to breach security barricades near Lok Bhavan.
key_points: The **Qaumi Insaaf Morcha** called a statewide bandh from **7 AM to 2 PM**, backed by the influential **Shiromani Gurdwara Parbandhak Committee (SGPC)**
The core demand: release **Sikh prisoners ('Bandi Singhs')** the Morcha says have already **completed their sentences** but remain jailed
Schools, colleges, shops, factories, buses and highways across Punjab were shut or disrupted during the bandh window
The protest follows an **August 15** clash near the Chandigarh–Mohali border, where police used **tear gas and water cannons** on demonstrators
Punjab Governor **Gulab Chand Kataria** was the target of the earlier march, which was blocked at barricades near Lok Bhavan

depth.background: '**Bandi Singhs**' refers to a group of Sikh prisoners, some convicted decades ago in cases tied to militancy and violence in Punjab during the 1980s-90s insurgency period, whom Sikh religious and political organizations say have already served sentences equivalent to a life term, yet remain in custody. Their release has been a recurring, emotionally charged demand in Punjab and among Sikh communities globally, periodically flaring into major protests. The **Qaumi Insaaf Morcha** ('National Justice Front') is a coalition of Sikh organizations pushing specifically on this issue, and its campaigns have previously drawn support from mainstream religious bodies like the **SGPC**, which administers Sikh gurdwaras (temples) across Punjab.

cards.title: India moves to collapse GST into just two tax slabs, promising cheaper daily essentials
cards.what_happened: On **August 20**, Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman attended a meeting of the state-ministers' panel (the **GoM**) to walk through the Centre's proposal for restructuring GST. The core idea: shrink the current multi-slab structure down to just **two main rates, 5% and 18%**, with a **40% special rate** reserved for a short list of luxury or "sin" goods such as tobacco and high-end cars. Sitharaman described the exercise as a "**system-cleaning reform**" — the aim is fewer disputes over which rate applies where, and lower sticker prices on goods that move from a higher slab, like 12% or 28%, down into the new 5% or 18% bands. The proposal builds directly on PM Modi's August 15 Independence Day pledge to deliver "next-generation" GST reforms. The plan is not final: it still needs the **full GST Council** — which includes every state's finance minister plus the Centre — to formally approve the new rate structure before it takes effect.
key_points: Finance Minister **Nirmala Sitharaman** presented the Centre's plan to a panel of state ministers on **August 20** to simplify India's Goods and Services Tax.
The proposal collapses today's multiple GST slabs into just **two main rates — 5% and 18%** — plus a **40% special rate** for a handful of luxury/sin items.
It follows PM **Modi's Independence Day announcement** on August 15 of "next-generation" GST reforms.
The stated goal is a **"system-cleaning" reform** that lowers prices on everyday goods and cuts compliance headaches for businesses.
The plan still needs sign-off from the full **GST Council** — the state-and-centre body that has final say — before it becomes law.

depth.background: India's GST — the single nationwide tax that replaced a maze of state and central taxes in 2017 — has long been criticized for having **too many rate slabs** (5%, 12%, 18%, 28%, plus special rates), which makes compliance confusing and invites disputes over which rate applies to which product. The government has periodically simplified it since; this latest push is being pitched as the next big leap — **"GST 2.0"** — squeezing most goods into just two main brackets. It was set in motion when PM Modi flagged "next-generation" GST reform in his **Independence Day speech from the Red Fort** on August 15, and the **Group of Ministers (GoM)**, a panel of state finance ministers who negotiate rate changes before the full GST Council votes, met on August 20 to go through the Centre's specific proposal.

cards.title: Gold and silver platform Augmont Enterprises opens its ₹825-crore IPO today
cards.what_happened: Augmont Enterprises Limited's IPO opened for public subscription today, August 21, and will close on August 25. The company is offering shares in a price band of **₹750 to ₹788**, aiming to raise up to **₹825 crore** through the main-board listing on the NSE and BSE. Ahead of the public opening, the company's anchor book — the portion sold to large institutional investors a day before the retail opening — was **oversubscribed, raising ₹246 crore**. The minimum retail investment works out to roughly ₹14,972 for a lot of 19 shares at the upper price band. Nuvama Wealth Management is the lead book-running manager, with listing tentatively expected around August 31.
key_points: Augmont's IPO opens today with a price band of **₹750–₹788 per share**
The issue aims to raise up to **₹825 crore**, closing August 25
Anchor investors have already committed **₹246 crore** ahead of the public opening
Augmont is an **integrated gold and silver platform** serving businesses and retail buyers across India
The listing lands in the middle of a **hot IPO season** already covered by Tempsens and Lalithaa Jewellery's oversubscribed issues

depth.background: An **Initial Public Offering (IPO)** is when a private company sells shares to the public for the first time to raise money and get listed on a stock exchange. Before the public opening, companies typically sell a chunk of shares to large institutional **anchor investors** at a fixed price — strong anchor demand is often read as a vote of confidence that helps set the tone for retail investors. Augmont Enterprises, incorporated in 2012, runs an integrated **gold and silver platform** — effectively infrastructure connecting bullion supply, storage, and digital gold/silver products for businesses and consumers, in a country where gold buying is a deep cultural and financial habit.

cards.title: RBI survey: Indians grow warier about jobs and prices, even as they stay upbeat on their own income
cards.what_happened: The RBI released the July 2026 round of its household surveys on Wednesday, showing that consumer sentiment on the broader economy, employment prospects, and price levels **weakened compared to the previous round**. At the same time, households' views on their own personal income growth and spending plans **held up and stayed positive** — a split between how people see the country's economic direction versus their own household finances. The survey drew responses from urban households across 19 cities and rural households across 31 states and union territories.
key_points: RBI's July survey found households turned **more cautious about the broader economy, jobs, and inflation**
Despite that, respondents stayed **optimistic about their own income growth and spending**
The survey covers **19 cities** (urban) and **31 states/UTs** (rural) via RBI's confidence indices
Results were released **the same week as RBI's hawkish August policy minutes**, adding to rate-outlook debate
The findings feed directly into the **Monetary Policy Committee's** thinking on interest rates

thread.previously: We reported that the RBI's August policy minutes showed a hawkish tilt, rattling India's bond market and putting the possibility of rate hikes back on the table.
thread.changed: New household survey data shows consumer sentiment on the economy and inflation has also weakened, giving the RBI's hawkish stance fresh supporting evidence from the ground.

depth.background: Every two months, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) surveys thousands of households through its **Urban Consumer Confidence Survey**, **Rural Consumer Confidence Survey**, and **Inflation Expectations Survey of Households** — asking ordinary people how they feel about jobs, prices, and their own finances, both right now and a year ahead. These aren't hard economic data; they're a **sentiment gauge** the RBI uses alongside official statistics to judge whether consumers are pulling back or spending confidently, which feeds into decisions on interest rates. This round adds context to the RBI's already-hawkish August policy minutes covered in this feed, which pointed to interest rate hikes being back on the table.

cards.title: Elon Musk's Starlink reapplies to India's space regulator for a 30,000-satellite Gen 2 network
cards.what_happened: Starlink has filed a **fresh application** with IN-SPACe seeking approval for its next-generation **Gen 2** satellite constellation — roughly **30,000 satellites**, more than six times the size of its already-approved Gen 1 network. The new filing includes **direct-to-device connectivity**, technology that would let satellites talk directly to regular smartphones without any special dish or antenna. This is Starlink's second attempt at Gen 2 approval in India: its first application was turned down because some of its proposed features and frequency bands clashed with Indian telecom regulations. Right now, no non-geostationary satellite operator — not Starlink, not rival **Eutelsat OneWeb**, not the Reliance-Jio/SES joint venture — has actually begun commercial satellite-internet service in India, largely because security clearances and spectrum pricing are still unresolved across the industry.
key_points: Starlink has resubmitted its application to **IN-SPACe**, India's space regulator, for its **Gen 2** satellite constellation.
The new bid covers nearly **30,000 low-Earth-orbit satellites**, flying at **340-615 km altitude**.
It includes **direct-to-device (D2D)** tech — letting satellites connect straight to ordinary mobile phones, no special equipment needed.
Starlink's **first Gen 2 application was rejected** — some features and frequency bands didn't meet Indian rules.
Only its smaller **Gen 1 network (4,408 satellites)** has been cleared so far, back in **July 2025** — and still isn't commercially live.

depth.background: **Starlink**, owned by Elon Musk's SpaceX, beams internet down from thousands of satellites orbiting close to Earth (**low-Earth orbit**, or LEO) instead of relying on cables or ground towers — useful for reaching remote areas ordinary broadband can't. India has been a difficult market to crack: the government requires foreign satellite operators to clear security, spectrum (radio frequency), and pricing approvals through **IN-SPACe**, the national space regulator, before they can operate. Starlink's smaller Gen 1 constellation got the green light over a year ago, in July 2025, but still hasn't launched commercial service in India — showing how slow this approval pipeline can be even after a plan is technically cleared.

cards.title: Sensor maker Tempsens opens a ₹650-crore share sale and is six times covered on day one
cards.what_happened: Tempsens Instruments (India) opened its share sale for bidding on **Thursday 20 August 2026**, and by the end of the first day the issue was **5.95 times subscribed**. The breakdown was lopsided: the **non-institutional** bucket of wealthy individual investors was covered **12.51 times**, **retail** **6.48 times**, and the **institutional** bucket just **0.05 times** — as is typical on day one. The offer totals **₹650 crore**, made up of a **fresh issue of ₹95 crore** that goes to the company itself and an **offer for sale of ₹555 crore**, which is existing shareholders cashing out rather than new money for the business. The price band is **₹285 to ₹300 per share**, with a lot size of **50 shares**, so the smallest application is about **₹15,000**. Bidding closes on **24 August**, allotment is expected **25 August**, and the shares are due to list on the BSE and NSE on **28 August**.
key_points: Issue was **5.95 times subscribed** on day one
Wealthy individual investors bid **12.51x**; retail **6.48x**; institutions only **0.05x**
Total size **₹650 crore** — **₹95 crore** new money, **₹555 crore** sold by existing owners
Price band **₹285–₹300** a share; minimum application about **₹15,000**
Bidding closes **24 August**, listing expected **28 August**

depth.background: An **IPO (initial public offering)** is the moment a private company first sells shares to the public and lists on a stock exchange. In India, the offer is split into buckets: **retail** (ordinary small investors), **NII/HNI** (wealthy individuals and firms bidding large amounts) and **QIB** (qualified institutional buyers — mutual funds, insurers, foreign funds). **Subscription** counts how many times over the shares on offer have been bid for; **5.95x** means investors asked for nearly six shares for every one available. Institutions almost always bid on the final day, so a near-zero QIB number on day one is normal, not a warning. **Tempsens Instruments (India)**, founded in **1990**, makes temperature sensors, electrical heating systems and specialised cables — unglamorous industrial hardware that sits inside factories, steel plants and power stations.

cards.title: SEBI will pilot putting corporate bonds on a shared digital ledger, working with the RBI
cards.what_happened: **Amarjeet Singh**, a whole-time member of the **Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI)** — the regulator for India's stock and bond markets — said on **Thursday 20 August 2026** that SEBI will run a pilot to test **tokenisation of bonds**. The pilot will examine whether a **shared ledger** can allow the security and the cash to transfer **simultaneously**, removing the reconciliation step that sits between the two today. It will also test whether **coupon payments** — the regular interest a bond pays its holder — and other servicing events can be handled automatically by **smart contracts**, which are small programs that execute a payment when a pre-set condition is met. Crucially, the pilot is being run **in coordination with the Reserve Bank of India**, because the cash leg of any settlement sits under the central bank's remit, not SEBI's. SEBI framed the effort as part of a wider push to build a **deeper corporate bond repo market** — the short-term market in which bonds are used as collateral for cash loans, and which is what gives a bond market day-to-day liquidity.
key_points: SEBI whole-time member **Amarjeet Singh** announced the pilot on **Thursday**
It will test **tokenised bonds** — bond ownership recorded on a shared digital ledger
**Automated coupon payments** via smart contracts are part of the trial
Run **in coordination with the RBI**, so securities and money can move together
Aim is a **deeper corporate bond repo market** and lower reconciliation costs

depth.background: India's stock market is deep and liquid; its **corporate bond market is not**. A corporate bond is simply a loan to a company that can be bought and sold, but in India most bonds are bought and then held to maturity, so there are few buyers and sellers on any given day. One reason is plumbing: settling a bond trade means one system updating who owns the security and a separate system moving the cash, with people reconciling the two afterwards. **Tokenisation** means recording ownership as an entry on a **shared digital ledger** that all parties see at once, so the security and the money can change hands in the same instant. Regulators worldwide have been running versions of this experiment for several years; India is now joining with a supervised pilot rather than a free-for-all.

cards.title: SEBI scraps notarization hurdles for foreign investors, easing the door into Indian markets
cards.what_happened: SEBI **streamlined the onboarding process** for foreign portfolio investors by permitting the use of **digitally signed power-of-attorney documents**, eliminating the earlier requirement for **notarization and consularization**. The new regulations are set to **take effect on August 20, 2026**. In practice, an overseas fund that wants to invest in India can now complete a key piece of its registration paperwork **electronically**, rather than shipping physical documents abroad for stamps and consulate verification. The move lands at a moment when Indian markets are **wary** — domestic bonds have been under pressure after the RBI's hawkish policy minutes and rising oil prices — so making it simpler for foreign money to enter is timely. It is a technical, plumbing-level reform rather than a headline stimulus, but it lowers a real barrier that funds have long complained about.
key_points: New rules let foreign investors use **digitally signed** power-of-attorney documents.
The old requirement to **notarize and consularize** paperwork is dropped.
The change takes effect **August 20, 2026**.
Aim: cut red tape and **speed up onboarding** of foreign portfolio investors.
Comes as India courts **foreign inflows** amid a jittery bond market.

depth.background: **SEBI** is the Securities and Exchange Board of India — the regulator that polices the country's stock and bond markets, similar to the SEC in the US. **Foreign portfolio investors (FPIs)** are overseas funds that buy Indian stocks and bonds; their money is a big swing factor for Indian markets, so making it easier for them to register matters. Until now, an FPI's legal paperwork — like a **power of attorney** (a document authorizing someone to act on your behalf) — had to be **notarized** and **consularized** (stamped by a notary and then verified by an Indian consulate abroad), a slow, costly process. Cutting that friction is part of a broader push to make India a more welcoming, competitive destination for global capital.

cards.title: Omar Abdullah rebuffs US envoy Sergio Gor ahead of his Kashmir visit: 'Our problems won't be solved in Washington'
cards.what_happened: Hours before Gor arrived, **Omar Abdullah** publicly stated that J&K's problems **'don't have to be resolved in Washington'** — they **'have to be resolved by our own central government'** — signaling he had no intention of taking grievances to a foreign diplomat. Gor went ahead with the visit, meeting **Lieutenant Governor Manoj Sinha**, and praised the region's beauty, describing J&K as **'an important part of India.'** He also suggested the **US government's travel advisory** warning Americans about the region should be **downgraded**, which would be a boost for local tourism. The exchange captured the careful choreography around any foreign official's presence in the territory.
key_points: US Ambassador **Sergio Gor** made his **first visit to Jammu & Kashmir** since taking charge.
J&K CM **Omar Abdullah** said the region's problems are for **India's own government** to fix.
Gor met **Lt Governor Manoj Sinha** and called J&K 'an important part of India'.
Gor suggested the **US travel advisory** for J&K should be **downgraded**.
The visit spotlights the **delicate line** between diplomacy and internal politics.

depth.background: Jammu & Kashmir is a sensitive border region whose politics India treats firmly as an **internal matter**, wary of any outside 'mediation'. **Omar Abdullah** is the region's elected Chief Minister; **Sergio Gor** is the newly installed US Ambassador to India, who also carries responsibility for **South and Central Asia**. A foreign ambassador touring J&K is always closely watched, because New Delhi is protective of the message it sends. Gor's trip is the first such high-profile US visit since he took office.

cards.title: India clears field trials of 1 billion ₹10 and ₹20 polymer banknotes
cards.what_happened: India's government told **Parliament** it has cleared the **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** to conduct **field trials of one billion polymer banknotes each in the ₹10 and ₹20 denominations**. Officials stressed the goal is to **extend the lifespan** of small notes that wear out fastest, **reduce long-term printing costs**, and cut environmental waste. Crucially, they clarified there is **no plan to replace paper currency** — the polymer notes would circulate **alongside** existing paper notes, not instead of them. The move follows international studies showing polymer notes are significantly more durable than paper.
key_points: The government approved the **RBI's plan** to field-test **plastic (polymer) notes**.
The trial covers **one billion notes each** of **₹10 and ₹20**.
Aim: notes that **last far longer** than paper, cutting reprinting costs.
Paper currency **will continue** alongside — no plan to replace it.
Small notes wear out fastest, so they're the natural test case.

depth.background: Low-value notes like **₹10 and ₹20** change hands constantly, so they get grubby and torn quickly and have to be reprinted often — which is expensive and wasteful. **Polymer notes** are made of a thin, durable plastic film instead of cotton-paper; countries like Australia and the UK already use them because they **last two to three times longer** and are harder to counterfeit. India has floated the idea before (going back years) but never rolled it out at scale. This decision moves it from proposal to an actual **field trial** — a real-world test in limited circulation.

cards.title: RBI's hawkish August minutes rattle India's bond market, putting rate hikes back on the table
cards.what_happened: Minutes from the RBI's early-August policy meeting, released this week, showed a **notably more hawkish tone** than the headline decision suggested. While the MPC left the repo rate unchanged at **5.25%** for a fourth consecutive meeting, the minutes revealed that roughly half the committee is now leaning toward raising rates rather than holding or cutting them, driven by rising concern about inflation. That shift caught investors off guard, since markets had been positioned for steady-to-lower rates. The **10-year government security yield** climbed to roughly **6.78%** and the **rupee slid past ₹95 to the dollar** as traders repriced the odds of tighter policy ahead. The RBI's own projections show it expects **CPI inflation** to rise through the year — from 4.7% in the second quarter to 5.9% in the third and 5.5% in the fourth — even as it raised its full-year **GDP growth forecast to 6.7%** from 6.6%, citing resilient consumer demand and strong exports.
key_points: Minutes from the RBI's August meeting show members growing more worried about **inflation risk**, opening the door to **rate hikes** despite holding the repo rate at **5.25%** for a fourth straight meeting.
Roughly **half the committee** now leans toward tightening policy ahead, a sharp reversal from the market's expectation of steady or falling rates.
The **10-year government bond yield** rose to around **6.78%** on the news.
The **rupee weakened past ₹95 per US dollar** as investors repriced the odds of higher borrowing costs.
The RBI still raised its **FY2026 GDP growth forecast to 6.7%**, citing resilient domestic demand and robust exports.

depth.background: The **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** is India's central bank — its six-member **Monetary Policy Committee (MPC)** meets roughly every two months to set the **repo rate**, the interest rate at which it lends to commercial banks, which ripples through to loan and deposit rates across the economy. For most of this year the MPC has held rates steady, betting that inflation would stay contained while growth held up. The committee's published minutes — released with a lag after each meeting — are closely watched because they reveal the internal debate behind the headline decision, often moving markets more than the decision itself.

prev_ref.title: Tata Sons to reconvene its adjourned AGM within a week, as lawyers scramble to fix a century-old first

cards.title: Chandrasekaran confirms he won't seek another term as Tata Sons chairman, as the century-old AGM deadlock traces to a frozen trust
cards.what_happened: Tata Sons' annual general meeting, originally scheduled for August 18, was **adjourned for lack of quorum** — a first in the company's roughly 110-year history — because **Sir Ratan Tata Trusts (SRTT)**, which owns 23.56% of Tata Sons, could not validly nominate a representative while its own board composition remains disputed. That procedural failure has now been paired with a leadership answer: Chandrasekaran has confirmed he will **not seek another term** as chairman, and will continue only until his current tenure expires on **February 20, 2027**. The rescheduled AGM — expected to convene within about a week — will need to both resolve the quorum problem and formally process Chandrasekaran's succession, all before a mid-November statutory filing deadline. The dispute traces back to earlier tension between Chandrasekaran and Noel Tata, who had raised concerns over the performance of some of the Tata Group's newer ventures.
key_points: **N Chandrasekaran** has confirmed he will **not seek reappointment** as Tata Sons chairman, staying only until his current term ends on **February 20, 2027**.
Tata Sons' AGM was adjourned on August 18 for the **first time in the company's roughly 110-year history**, after failing to meet quorum.

The quorum failure traces to **Sir Ratan Tata Trusts (SRTT)**, which holds a **23.56% stake** in Tata Sons, being unable to validly nominate a representative amid a dispute over the trust's own board.
The underlying rift is between Chandrasekaran and **Tata Trusts chairman Noel Tata**, who has raised concerns over the performance of some of the group's newer businesses.
The board is expected to reconvene the AGM within about a week, racing a mid-November statutory deadline.

cards.title: Sensex and Nifty snap a seven-day losing streak as global bond jitters ease
cards.what_happened: The **BSE Sensex** and **NSE Nifty 50** staged a strong recovery on **Thursday**, snapping a **seven-day losing streak**. The Sensex gained **628 points (0.82%)** to close at **77,537.72**, while the Nifty rose **154 points (0.64%)** to **24,231.85**. The rally was driven by **easing concerns over US bond yields**, short covering (traders buying back stocks they had bet against), and fresh buying in large heavyweight stocks. **Foreign Institutional Investors (FIIs)**, who had been selling, turned net buyers, purchasing **₹407.99 crore** of Indian equities in the prior session.
