cards.title: Odisha announces ₹1,000-crore flood relief package as toll from record rains mounts
cards.what_happened: Odisha Chief Minister **Mohan Majhi** announced a **₹1,000-crore special relief package** on Thursday for people affected by the state's worst flooding in years. The floods have hit **over 9.4 lakh people** across **1,381 villages** in **74 blocks** spanning **six districts**, with more than **3.7 lakh people evacuated** to safer locations. **550 relief camps** have been set up to provide food and shelter, backed by **45 ODRAF teams, 8 NDRF teams, and 65 Fire Services teams**. Under the new package, farmers who lost **33% or more** of their crops will get an agricultural input subsidy for up to two hectares of land. The state has recorded **1,100mm of rainfall** since June — about **34% above normal** and the highest total in **25 years**.
key_points: Odisha's government announced a **₹1,000-crore relief package** for flood-hit families
Over **9.4 lakh people** across **1,381 villages** in **six districts** have been affected
More than **3.7 lakh people** have been evacuated, with **550 relief camps** now running
The state has received **1,100mm of rain** since June — **34% above normal** and the highest in **25 years**

thread.previously: We reported that a depression system from the Bay of Bengal was pushing floodwaters into parts of Odisha, cutting off villages, with more rain still expected.
thread.changed: Odisha's government has now announced a ₹1,000-crore relief package after confirming over 9.4 lakh people across six districts have been affected, with more than 3.7 lakh people evacuated.

depth.background: Odisha has been battered by an unusually intense monsoon this year, driven by a slow-moving depression system that formed over the Bay of Bengal and has repeatedly dumped heavy rain on the state. Farmers, already dealing with earlier flooding this season, have seen crops wiped out for a second time in some districts, and rescue teams have been stretched thin evacuating cut-off villages.

cards.title: Gold races toward record highs in India, crossing ₹1.58 lakh per 10 grams
cards.what_happened: Gold prices in India pushed toward record territory in trading today, with 24-carat gold crossing **₹1.55 lakh per 10 grams** nationally and the MCX October futures contract touching an intraday high of **₹1,58,750** (22-carat gold traded near ₹1,45,191). Silver also surged, up more than ₹4,000 on the day. The move follows a decline in **US bond yields** after the US Treasury announced it would double its buyback of long-term securities, making non-yielding gold comparatively more attractive to investors, layered on top of ongoing safe-haven demand tied to the **Strait of Hormuz/Iran-US standoff** and volatile global markets. Gold is now up over 10% in the past month and more than 59% over the past year, though still below its all-time high of ₹1,69,349 set on March 2, 2026.
key_points: **24-carat gold crossed ₹1.55 lakh** per 10 grams nationally, with MCX futures touching an intraday high near **₹1,58,750**.
Silver jumped too, rising over **₹4,000** on the day.
Gold is now up more than **10% in the past month** and over **59% over the past year** — still short of its March all-time high of ₹1,69,349.
The rally is being driven by **falling US bond yields** (after the US Treasury doubled its buyback of long-term debt) and safe-haven buying tied to **Strait of Hormuz tensions**.
Dealers say record prices are **dampening actual jewelry demand** even as investment demand stays strong.

depth.background: Gold tends to rise when investors get nervous about the world economy or geopolitics, because unlike a stock or bond it pays no interest but also can't default — making it a classic 'safe haven.' It also tends to rise when interest rates or bond yields fall, since gold competes with interest-bearing assets for investors' money and looks relatively more attractive when those yields drop. India is one of the world's largest gold buyers, especially around weddings and festivals, so price moves like this ripple directly into household budgets, not just investment portfolios.

cards.title: SEBI bars a JPMorgan unit and a Mumbai broker for rigging the Sensex's brand-new closing-price mechanism
cards.what_happened: SEBI passed an emergency ('ex-parte') interim order against **Copthall Mauritius Investment Limited**, a unit of **JPMorgan Chase & Co**, and **Mansi Share and Stock Broking Private Limited**, barring both from accessing Indian securities markets and impounding **₹3.67 crore** in alleged wrongful gains — about ₹2.96 crore from Copthall and ₹71.64 lakh from Mansi. The order concerns trading on **August 13, 2026**, a Sensex weekly options-expiry day, during the new Closing Auction Session. Both firms held Sensex options positions that would profit if the index closed higher. SEBI's order says Copthall placed extremely aggressive buy orders between 3:21pm and 3:25pm — accounting for **99.91% of buy-order value** in the first price spike — pushing prices about 3% above their reference level, while Mansi simultaneously placed large sell orders, then cancelled the entire quantity within seconds, a sequence SEBI flagged as a coordinated attempt to move the closing price. The order was signed by SEBI whole-time member Kamlesh Chandra Varshney.
key_points: India's market regulator **SEBI barred Copthall Mauritius** (a JPMorgan Chase unit) and **Mansi Share and Stock Broking** from the markets, impounding **₹3.67 crore** in alleged illegal gains.
It's the **first enforcement action** under India's new **Closing Auction Session (CAS)**, introduced just weeks ago on August 3 to stop exactly this kind of price-gaming.

SEBI says on **August 13**, Copthall placed aggressive buy orders — **99.91% of buy value** in one price spike — while Mansi placed and then abruptly cancelled large sell orders, together pushing the Sensex close ~3% off its natural level.
Both firms held **Sensex options** that would profit from exactly the price move they allegedly engineered.
It follows SEBI chief **Tuhin Kanta Pandey's public warning just a day earlier** that manipulating the new CAS would draw 'strict action'.

depth.background: India's stock exchanges long used a simpler method to set a stock or index's official 'closing price,' which traders could game by placing large orders in the final seconds of trading to move the close in their favor — a loophole regulators cracked down on after the high-profile **Jane Street case**, where a global trading firm was banned for allegedly doing exactly this. To fix it, SEBI introduced the **Closing Auction Session (CAS)** on August 3, 2026: a 20-minute window (3:15–3:35pm) where the closing price is set through a fairer auction process rather than the last trade. This case is the first real test of whether that fix actually works.

cards.title: India's newest stock listings are outperforming even as the overall IPO boom cools
cards.what_happened: New data shows that six companies which listed on Indian exchanges in August have seen their share prices climb between **9% and 81%** above their issue price, even as the broader Nifty 50 has been sliding for multiple sessions. **Behari Lal Engineering** became the latest example, debuting today with shares opening at **₹465** on the NSE — a **63.1% premium** to its issue price — and **₹458** on the BSE, up **60.7%**. This comes against a backdrop where India's total IPO fundraising for 2026 has fallen to about **$5.78 billion**, down roughly a fifth from **$7.32 billion** in the same period last year, after two record years in 2024 and 2025. Analysts at Goldman Sachs and JPMorgan still expect full-year 2026 proceeds to land above **$20 billion**, with Kotak Mahindra Capital and Goldman projecting up to **$25 billion**, partly on the strength of a pipeline that includes Reliance Jio, SBI Mutual Fund, PhonePe, boAt, Flipkart, and NSE's own long-awaited listing.
key_points: Six companies that listed on Indian exchanges in **August alone** have rallied between **9% and 81%** above their issue price.
**Behari Lal Engineering** debuted today with shares opening at a **63% premium** on the NSE and **61% premium** on the BSE.
Overall IPO fundraising is actually down about a fifth this year to roughly **$5.78 billion**, from record years of **$22.36 billion in 2025** and **$20.65 billion in 2024**.
Companies are **cutting deal sizes and accepting lower valuations** to get deals done, even as the listings themselves pop on debut.
Big-ticket IPOs still expected before year-end include **PhonePe, boAt, Flipkart, and the National Stock Exchange (NSE)** itself.

depth.background: India has just come off two record-breaking years for initial public offerings (IPOs — when a private company first sells shares to the public), with companies raising over $20 billion in both 2024 and 2025 as investors piled into India's growing economy. That pace has slowed sharply in 2026: with broader Indian markets under pressure from high oil prices and global bond yields, companies have been trimming how much they try to raise and accepting lower valuations just to get their listings done. Despite that caution at the fundraising stage, investor appetite for the shares once they actually start trading has stayed strong, creating an unusual split between a **cooling primary market** (new share sales) and a **hot secondary market** (trading once listed).

cards.title: Tata Sons' board splits over how to handle N Chandrasekaran's exit as chairman
cards.what_happened: N Chandrasekaran informed the Tata Sons board on **August 12** that he will not seek another term as chairman once his current tenure concludes on **February 20, 2027**. In the days since, the board has reportedly split over how to formally respond: some directors want to hold a **vote** to accept or reject that decision, while others believe he should be **persuaded to reconsider** and stay on. Separately, the **Sir Dorabji Tata Trust** — one of the two trusts that control Tata Sons — wrote to the board arguing that directors' duty now is to focus on succession planning, not on relitigating whether Chandrasekaran should stay, and has asked the board to begin constituting a **selection committee** to find his replacement. The board is expected to take up the matter formally at a meeting in **mid-September**.
key_points: Tata Sons chairman **N Chandrasekaran** told the board on **August 12** that he does not want another term when his tenure ends on **February 20, 2027**.
The board is now divided: some directors want the decision **put to a formal vote**, others want to **ask him to reconsider**.
The **Sir Dorabji Tata Trust** has written to the board urging it to accept the decision and start building a **selection committee** for his successor.
It follows a **February 24 board meeting** where four of six directors backed extending Chandrasekaran, but **Noel Tata** — chairman of Tata Trusts — did not support it.
Tata Sons' board is expected to meet again in **mid-September** to formally address the succession question.

depth.background: Tata Sons is the holding company that controls the sprawling Tata Group — from Tata Motors and Tata Steel to Air India and TCS — making its chairman one of the most powerful executives in Indian business. N Chandrasekaran has led Tata Sons since 2017, and Tata Sons' controlling shareholders are two charitable trusts (the Sir Dorabji Tata Trust and Sir Ratan Tata Trust), whose leadership effectively decides who runs the group. This succession question has been building since a **February 24, 2026** board meeting where a proposed five-year extension for Chandrasekaran failed to win unanimous backing, with Noel Tata — chairman of Tata Trusts and a Tata Sons board member — declining to support it. Tata Sons' Annual General Meeting was also separately disrupted this week by an unrelated regulatory issue blocking a trust representative from attending.

cards.title: Zerodha's Nikhil Kamath backs India's data-centre boom with a ₹250 crore bet on CtrlS
cards.what_happened: CtrlS Datacenters announced it raised **₹250 crore** in fresh funding, with Zerodha co-founder **Nikhil Kamath** contributing ₹200 crore and entrepreneur **Sreeram Reddy Vanga** adding ₹50 crore. The company said the capital will support its infrastructure expansion and capacity build-out to meet growing enterprise and hyperscale demand as AI, cloud, and digital workloads accelerate across India. CtrlS currently operates **19 data centres across nine Indian markets**, with more than **370 MW** of live capacity and roughly **4.4 GW** of additional projects at various stages of execution. The new investment follows the much larger ₹7,000 crore raise the company closed in June from CPP Investments, which valued CtrlS at **$4.7 billion**.
key_points: Zerodha co-founder **Nikhil Kamath** put in **₹200 crore**, entrepreneur **Sreeram Reddy Vanga** added **₹50 crore**
The money funds **CtrlS Datacenters'** expansion to meet **AI, cloud and hyperscale demand**
CtrlS runs **19 data centres** across **9 Indian markets**, with over **370 MW** of live capacity

depth.background: Data centres are the physical warehouses of servers that power cloud computing and AI — every AI chatbot query or streaming video runs through one. As companies race to build AI products, demand for the computing power, electricity, land and cooling that data centres provide has surged, and India is trying to position itself as a major hub for that build-out. **CtrlS**, founded in Hyderabad in 2007 by Sridhar Pinnapureddy, is one of India's largest data-centre operators and has raised large sums this year to expand, including a ₹7,000 crore round in June from Canada's pension fund, **CPP Investments**.

cards.title: Lalithaa Jewellery Mart's IPO closes nearly 8x oversubscribed
cards.what_happened: Lalithaa Jewellery Mart Ltd's **initial public offering (IPO)** closed for bidding on **August 19, 2026**, ending up subscribed **7.77 times** overall. The strongest demand came from **non-institutional investors**, who bid **22.45 times** their allotted portion, while **retail investors** subscribed **5.32 times** and employees **4.64 times**. The issue was priced at **₹190 to ₹201 per share**, and the **grey market premium** stood at **₹40**, implying an estimated listing price around **₹241** — roughly a **20% premium** to the top of the price band. Allotment is expected to be finalized on **August 20**, with the stock tentatively listing on the **NSE and BSE** on **August 24, 2026**.
key_points: Lalithaa Jewellery Mart's **IPO** closed on **August 19** overall subscribed **7.77 times**.
**Non-institutional investors** bid **22.45x** their allotted shares; retail investors bid **5.32x**.
The **grey market premium (GMP)** stood at **₹40**, pointing to a likely listing around **₹241** versus the ₹190–201 issue price band.
Allotment is expected **August 20**, with listing on the **NSE and BSE** tentatively set for **August 24**.

depth.background: Lalithaa Jewellery Mart is a South India-focused jewellery retail chain going public. Like most Indian IPOs, its shares were offered in a price band (**₹190 to ₹201**) and investors could bid across categories — retail individual investors (**RII**), non-institutional investors (**NII**, typically wealthier individuals and small funds), and employees. Before a stock lists, an unofficial 'grey market' often trades the right to shares at a premium or discount to the issue price, giving an early signal of investor appetite — that's the **grey market premium (GMP)**. This IPO comes as Indian markets have otherwise been jittery, with the Sensex and Nifty under pressure from costly oil and rising global bond yields.

cards.title: IMD warns of fresh flash floods and landslides across Himalayan states through August 24
cards.what_happened: The **IMD** issued warnings for intense rainfall in **Himachal Pradesh** from **August 19–21** and **Uttarakhand** from **August 20–24**, with broader alerts extending to **Jammu & Kashmir, Ladakh, Punjab, Haryana, Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh**, and **Vidarbha** through August 24. Separately, **Konkan, Goa, coastal Karnataka, and parts of Kerala** were flagged for heavy rain and gusty winds reaching **60 kmph** in Karnataka and Tamil Nadu. Fishermen along the **north Bay of Bengal** were advised to stay off the water. This is a distinct rain system from the Bengal depression driving the ongoing Odisha flooding, arriving while hill states are still on edge after Uttarakhand's deadly Chamoli tunnel collapse this past week.
key_points: India's weather office (**IMD**) issued fresh heavy-rain warnings for **Himachal Pradesh** (Aug 19–21) and **Uttarakhand** (Aug 20–24).
Wider alerts also cover **Jammu & Kashmir, Ladakh, Punjab, Haryana, Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh**, and **Vidarbha** through August 24.
Coastal states — **Konkan, Goa, coastal Karnataka, and Kerala** — face heavy rain and gusty winds up to **60 kmph**.

This is a **separate weather system** from the Bengal depression already flooding Odisha, hitting hill states still recovering from a deadly monsoon season, including Uttarakhand's fatal Chamoli tunnel collapse.

depth.background: India's monsoon (June–September) regularly brings intense, fast-moving rain systems, and this year has already been unusually deadly in the Himalayan belt — Uttarakhand just finished recovering the last bodies from a tunnel collapse in Chamoli, and hill states are prone to landslides when soil already soaked from earlier rain gets hit again. The **India Meteorological Department (IMD)** issues color-coded warnings as rain systems form, giving states time to evacuate low-lying and landslide-prone areas. This new warning is driven by a fresh weather system distinct from the Bengal depression currently flooding parts of Odisha further east.

cards.title: India's National Stock Exchange eyes a $55 billion IPO valuation, as rival BSE's shares lose favor
cards.what_happened: New reporting says NSE is now working toward an IPO that could value the exchange at roughly **$55 billion**, which would make it one of the largest listings in Indian corporate history. As the prospect of an actual NSE listing firms up, investors have started **selling down BSE shares**, since much of BSE's stock-price rally in recent years was driven by it being the only publicly tradeable way to bet on India's exchange sector. With NSE itself potentially becoming directly investable, that scarcity premium on BSE is fading. The move follows years of NSE working through regulatory requirements set by SEBI before it could proceed with a public offering.
key_points: The **National Stock Exchange (NSE)**, India's dominant stock exchange, is reportedly targeting a valuation of around **$55 billion** for its long-awaited IPO.
NSE handles the **vast majority of India's stock and derivatives trading volume**, dwarfing rival exchange BSE.
Investors have been rotating out of **BSE shares**, which had rallied hard on anticipation of NSE staying private — that trade is now unwinding.
An NSE listing has been **delayed for years** by regulatory and governance disputes with market regulator SEBI.
A successful listing would be one of **India's largest-ever IPOs**, a major event for the domestic stock market itself.

depth.background: The NSE is the engine room of India's stock market — most of the trading in stocks, derivatives, and index products happens on its platform, far more than on its older rival, the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE). Despite its dominance, NSE has stayed a private, unlisted company for years, even as market participants and its own shareholders pushed for a public listing to unlock its value and allow easier trading of its shares. That listing was repeatedly delayed by **unresolved regulatory issues** — including a long-running dispute with market regulator SEBI over past governance and technology lapses at the exchange. In the meantime, BSE — which is already publicly listed — became something of a proxy trade for investors who wanted exposure to India's exchange business without being able to buy NSE shares directly.

cards.title: India's Cabinet clears ₹13,000 crore for new highways and rail lines, with a fresh push on Bihar connectivity
cards.what_happened: India's Union Cabinet approved a package of infrastructure projects worth over **₹13,000 crore** on August 19. The **CCEA** cleared four railway 'multitracking' projects — adding extra parallel lines to existing routes to ease congestion — on the **Kharagpur-Bhadrak**, **Bhadrak-Haridaspur**, **Gummidipundi-Gudur**, and **Cuttack-Paradeep** sections, adding roughly **410 km** of track at a combined cost of **₹9,450 crore**, targeted for completion by **2030-31**. Separately, the Cabinet approved upgrading an **82.578 km** stretch of **NH-22** in Bihar — from Muzaffarpur to Sitamarhi to Sonbarsa on the India-Nepal border — into a four-lane highway under the **Hybrid Annuity Mode** (a public-private funding model), at a cost of **₹3,590.73 crore**. The project includes seven major bridges, including a 340-metre bridge over the Bagmati river, three rail overbridges, and two flyovers.
key_points: The Cabinet approved **four railway multitracking projects** adding **~410 km** of new track for **₹9,450 crore**
A separate **₹3,590.73 crore** project will turn an **82.578 km** stretch of NH-22 in Bihar into a four-lane highway
The Bihar highway connects the **India-Nepal border** at Sonbarsa to Muzaffarpur, a key economic corridor
It includes **seven major bridges** — including a **340-metre bridge** over the Bagmati river — plus flyovers and rail crossings
The railway projects span **West Bengal, Odisha, Tamil Nadu, and Andhra Pradesh**, targeted for completion by **2030-31**

depth.background: India's Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs (CCEA), chaired by PM **Narendra Modi**, regularly approves large infrastructure projects meant to cut freight and travel bottlenecks across the country — part of a long-running push to modernize India's railway and highway network to support faster economic growth. Bihar in particular has lagged behind other states on infrastructure investment, and projects that improve its connectivity to neighboring Nepal and to India's broader highway grid are politically and economically significant for one of India's poorest states.

cards.title: Shiprocket shares jump 35% on stock market debut, valuing the logistics startup at over ₹9,500 crore
cards.what_happened: **Shiprocket** made its stock market debut on August 19, with shares listing at **₹131** on the NSE — a **35% premium** over its **₹97 IPO issue price** — and at **₹129.50** on the BSE, a **33.5% gain**. The listing gives the company a market capitalization of roughly **₹9,531 crore**. The IPO, sized at **₹1,617.48 crore**, was open for subscription from **August 12 to 14** and was oversubscribed **99.38 times**, driven heavily by qualified institutional buyers who bid **122.80 times** their allotted portion. By midday trading, the stock had climbed further to around **₹139.50**, up nearly **44%** from the issue price.
key_points: Shiprocket listed at **₹131** on the NSE, a **35% premium** over its **₹97** issue price
The IPO was subscribed **99.38 times** overall, with institutional buyers alone bidding **122.80x** their share
The listing values Shiprocket at roughly **₹9,531 crore** (about $1.1 billion)
Shares climbed further after listing, touching **₹139.50** — up nearly **44%** from the issue price — within hours
The **₹1,617-crore IPO** was open for bidding from August 12–14

depth.background: Shiprocket is an e-commerce logistics and shipping platform that helps small and mid-sized online sellers in India manage delivery, tracking, and returns — the kind of backend infrastructure that boomed alongside India's e-commerce growth. Its IPO (**Initial Public Offering** — the first time a private company sells shares to the public and starts trading on a stock exchange) is one of several tech-adjacent listings testing investor appetite this year, at a time when India's benchmark indices have been sliding for days on unrelated global pressures (oil prices and US bond yields).

cards.title: India's Lakshya Sen crashes out of his home World Championships in Delhi, upset by an unseeded American
cards.what_happened: Playing at the **Indira Gandhi Arena** in New Delhi, Sen first survived a scare in the Round of 64, coming back from a game down to beat Austria's Collins Valentine Filimon **16-21, 21-8, 21-4**, crediting a tactical change for the turnaround. But in the **Round of 32**, unseeded American **Garret Tan** pulled off the upset, rallying from a game down to beat Sen and end his run at the home Championships. The loss means India's most closely-watched singles campaign at its own World Championships is over earlier than hoped, in the tournament's second round.
key_points: Sen lost his **Round of 32** match to unseeded American **Garret Tan** after winning the first game.
New Delhi is hosting the **BWF World Championships** for the first time since **2009**.
Sen was India's **biggest individual medal hope** in men's singles at the home tournament.
He had earlier survived a scare, coming back from a game down to beat Austria's **Collins Valentine Filimon**.
The tournament, at **Indira Gandhi Arena**, runs **August 17-23** with other Indian players still in the draw.

depth.background: The **BWF World Championships** is badminton's biggest annual event outside the Olympics, where the world's top singles and doubles players compete for the sport's most prestigious title. India is hosting the tournament for the first time in **17 years**, a significant moment for a sport that has grown rapidly in the country since stars like Saina Nehwal and PV Sindhu won Olympic medals last decade. **Lakshya Sen**, a former World Championship medalist and this year's **All England Open runner-up**, was widely seen as India's strongest hope for a men's singles medal in front of a home crowd.

cards.title: The rupee slides to a three-week low as oil nears $92 a barrel on Strait of Hormuz fears
cards.what_happened: The rupee fell to about **95.75 to the dollar** on Wednesday, its weakest level in three weeks, as Brent crude pushed up toward **$92 a barrel** — a more than 3% rise this week alone. The move tracks directly with the escalating US-Iran standoff: this week's expiry of the 60-day ceasefire deadline over the Strait of Hormuz, combined with President Trump's threats against Oman, has kept oil markets on edge. Currency traders say the **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** is standing by to intervene and cushion the fall, but some are now bracing for a slide toward the **96-per-dollar** level. The pressure builds on an already-jittery week after the RBI's own move to close a dollar-deposit swap facility for overseas Indians a month early, which had also weighed on sentiment.
key_points: The rupee weakened to around **95.75 per US dollar**, its **weakest level in three weeks**.
**Brent crude** climbed toward **$92 a barrel**, up over **3% this week**, as the US-Iran ceasefire deadline lapsed without a deal.
India imports roughly **85% of its crude oil**, so pricier oil directly widens the country's import bill.
Traders are watching for a possible slide toward **96 per dollar** even as the **RBI stands ready** to intervene and smooth volatility.
The move compounds pressure from the RBI's own decision last week to **end a dollar-swap facility a month early**, which had already unsettled currency sentiment.

depth.background: The Indian rupee's value against the US dollar is heavily influenced by the price of crude oil, because India buys the vast majority of the oil it uses from abroad — every dollar more per barrel means more dollars have to leave the country to pay for it, which weakens the rupee. That sensitivity has been on full display this month as the **US-Iran standoff over the Strait of Hormuz** — the narrow waterway through which roughly a fifth of the world's oil passes — has pushed crude prices higher and rattled global shipping.

cards.title: Tata Sons to reconvene its adjourned AGM within a week, as lawyers scramble to fix a century-old first
cards.what_happened: Tata Sons' AGM, originally scheduled for Tuesday August 18, was **adjourned for lack of quorum** — the first time this has happened in the company's roughly 110-year history — because SRTT's representative couldn't be validly nominated while the trust's powers are frozen. The meeting's agenda, including approving 2025-26 financial statements, declaring a dividend, and reappointing Chandrasekaran as chairman, is now on hold. Reporting today says Tata Sons' board plans to meet within about a week to set a fresh AGM date, and that legal advisers are actively working through options to resolve the deadlock, with the mid-November statutory deadline adding real time pressure. The rescheduled AGM will likely also be the venue where the board formally processes Chandrasekaran's resignation letter, adding a leadership question on top of the governance one.
key_points: Tata Sons' board is expected to convene **within about a week** to set a new AGM date after Tuesday's meeting collapsed for lack of quorum.
The deadlock traces to the **Sir Ratan Tata Trust (SRTT)**, whose power to nominate an AGM representative is **frozen by Maharashtra's Charity Commissioner** over a rule capping perpetual trustees.
Tata Sons' rules require **SRTT and the Sir Dorabji Tata Trust to jointly nominate** AGM representatives — with SRTT frozen, that nomination legally couldn't happen.
Law requires the AGM to be held within **15 months of the last one**, setting an effective deadline around **mid-November 2026**.
The rescheduled meeting will likely also formally address chairman **N. Chandrasekaran's** August 12 letter saying he won't seek a third term.

By law, the AGM must happen within 15 months of the last one — putting a hard deadline around mid-November.

That structure means the trusts' representatives normally have to formally show up and participate for the company's **annual general meeting (AGM)** — the yearly shareholder meeting that approves accounts, dividends and board appointments — to have the minimum attendance (**quorum**) needed to legally proceed. cards.title: Delhi's ex-minister Satyendar Jain arrested in a sewage-plant tender case, calls it 'Punjab poll politics'
cards.what_happened: The ACB arrested Satyendar Jain over alleged large-scale irregularities and criminal conspiracy in the tendering process for augmenting Delhi Jal Board's sewage treatment plants, part of an FIR originally registered in May 2024. He was one of six people arrested, alongside a former Delhi Jal Board CEO, a former IAS consultant, and contractors from two private firms. He was produced before Rouse Avenue Court a day after his arrest, where the court reserved its order on the ACB's request for judicial custody. Jain publicly alleged the timing was political, linking it to the approaching Punjab Assembly elections where his party currently governs.
key_points: **Satyendar Jain**, a senior AAP leader and former Delhi minister, was arrested by the **Anti-Corruption Branch (ACB)** and produced before Rouse Avenue Court
The case alleges **manipulation of tender conditions** for upgrading Delhi Jal Board's **Sewage Treatment Plants**
**Six people** were arrested in total, including a former Delhi Jal Board CEO and two private contractors, under an FIR first filed in **May 2024**
Jain says the arrest is **politically motivated**, tied to the upcoming **Punjab Assembly elections**, where his AAP governs
The court has **reserved its order** on whether to send Jain and the other accused to judicial custody

depth.background: Satyendar Jain is a founding-generation Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) leader who served as a Delhi minister and was previously jailed for over a year in a separate money-laundering case before getting bail. Delhi's Anti-Corruption Branch, which made this arrest, reports to the Delhi government but has been a recurring flashpoint between AAP and the BJP-run central government over who actually controls it. The case centers on the **Delhi Jal Board**, the city's water and sewage utility, and alleges irregularities in how contracts were awarded to upgrade its sewage treatment plants.

cards.title: Rescuers recover the last two bodies from Uttarakhand's Chamoli tunnel collapse, toll now at 10
cards.what_happened: On August 13, a landslide-triggered surge of water and debris flooded the under-construction tunnel at Hat-Siyasain, Mayapur-Pipalkoti, trapping 22 workers inside. Twelve were rescued with injuries in the days that followed as India's State Disaster Response Force (SDRF) and National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) mounted an intensive search-and-rescue operation. Bodies were recovered in stages over the following days, and on August 18 the last two — identified as Lukas Topno and Chetan Poyam — were found, bringing the confirmed death toll to 10 and formally concluding the search operation.
key_points: The bodies of **Lukas Topno** (31, from Jharkhand) and **Chetan Poyam** (from Chhattisgarh) were the last of **22 trapped workers** to be found
A landslide flooded the tunnel with debris and water on **August 13**, at a hydro-project site near the Birhi river
**12 workers were rescued** with injuries; the confirmed death toll now stands at **10**
The tunnel belongs to the **Vishnugad-Pipalkoti hydroelectric project**, run by state-owned THDC India
**SDRF and NDRF** teams, working what officials called a war-footing operation, have formally concluded the search

depth.background: Uttarakhand's stretch of the Himalayas is geologically young and prone to sudden landslides, especially during the monsoon, which makes large infrastructure projects there — like hydroelectric dams and their access tunnels — inherently risky to build. The workforce on such projects is often made up of migrant laborers from poorer states like Jharkhand and Chhattisgarh, who take on dangerous jobs far from home. The August 13 accident happened inside a **three-kilometre tunnel** under construction for the Vishnugad-Pipalkoti hydro project when a landslide near the Birhi river sent a sudden surge of debris and water inside, trapping the 22 workers who were on shift.

cards.title: India's biggest IT firms shed nearly 7,000 jobs this year as AI forces a hiring reset
cards.what_happened: A Business Standard review of FY26 hiring data shows India's five largest IT companies posted a combined headcount contraction of **6,981 employees**, compared with an increase of 12,798 the year before — a sharp reversal driven largely by roughly **23,000 job cuts at TCS** and slower growth elsewhere. A separate Nomura study tracking AI's employment impact since 2023 found the country added 83,100 AI-related roles against about 32,900 jobs lost to AI adoption, meaning AI has been a net job creator so far — but the study also found the new roles rarely go to the same people whose jobs were automated away. More than half the IT firms surveyed said entry-level and junior positions have specifically shrunk over the past two years, as AI tools absorb routine coding, testing and support work that used to be how graduates got their start. In response, companies are pivoting from external hiring toward large-scale internal reskilling programs, even as a shortage of AI-ready talent makes specialist recruitment slower and more expensive.
key_points: India's top five IT firms — **TCS, Infosys, HCL Tech, Wipro, and Tech Mahindra** — together cut headcount by **6,981 jobs** in FY26, versus adding nearly 12,800 the year before.
A Nomura study found India created **83,100 AI-related jobs** since 2023 but lost roughly **32,900** to AI — a net gain, but in different roles than the ones it destroyed.
**55% of IT companies** say entry-level hiring has shrunk over the last two years, as AI tools take over junior coding and support work.
Firms are shifting from mass hiring to **reskilling at scale**, retraining existing staff instead of only recruiting new AI talent.
A shortage of "industry-ready" AI specialists is slowing the rebound even as demand for AI skills rises.

depth.background: India's IT services industry has for decades been the country's biggest white-collar job engine, hiring hundreds of thousands of engineering graduates every year on the promise of steady, predictable growth. That model is now colliding with generative AI tools that can write, test, and debug code — tasks that used to be the entry point for fresh graduates. Industry leaders like TCS, Infosys, Wipro, HCL Tech and Tech Mahindra have spent much of 2026 talking publicly about "AI-first" strategies while simultaneously trimming headcount for the first time in years.

cards.title: The Bengal depression is now flooding parts of Odisha, cutting off villages as more rain looms
cards.what_happened: The depression that prompted yesterday's red alert has now moved inland and was centered over Jharkhand and northern Gangetic West Bengal as of 8:30 AM today, continuing to track west-northwest toward Bihar. In Odisha, incessant rainfall has already triggered flood-like conditions in the Subarnapur and Keonjhar districts, with several areas cut off due to waterlogged and submerged roads; Bahalda recorded **273mm** of rain. The IMD has an orange warning active for Sundargarh, Jharsuguda, Bargarh and Sambalpur, and a yellow warning for Deogarh, Angul, Keonjhar, Mayurbhanj, Subarnapur, Boudh and Bolangir. The system itself is expected to weaken into a well-marked low-pressure area within 24 hours as it continues across Jharkhand and Bihar, but the IMD is already warning of a fresh rainfall pulse from **August 22 to 24**, which could hit the same catchment areas before they've had time to drain.
key_points: The depression was centered over **Jharkhand and northern Gangetic West Bengal** at 8:30 AM today, moving west-northwest.
**Flood-like conditions** have hit Odisha's Subarnapur and Keonjhar districts, cutting off several villages.
An **orange warning** (heavy to very heavy rain) is active for Sundargarh, Jharsuguda, Bargarh and Sambalpur in Odisha.
The system is expected to **weaken into a low-pressure area** over the next 24 hours as it crosses Jharkhand and Bihar.

depth.background: This depression formed over the Bay of Bengal earlier this week and is part of India's annual monsoon system, where low-pressure areas regularly form over the Bay and move inland, dumping heavy rain across eastern India. Odisha, Jharkhand, Bihar and West Bengal sit directly in the path of these systems and see this pattern repeat several times every monsoon season, but back-to-back systems (like the second pulse now forecast for Aug 22-24) are what tend to turn manageable rain into real flooding, since the ground and rivers don't get time to drain between spells.

cards.title: India's telecom giants are quietly softening you up for a big price hike later this year
cards.what_happened: Instead of announcing a headline price increase, Bharti Airtel has quietly discontinued several popular prepaid packs, including its ₹299 entry-level plan and its ₹319, ₹579 and ₹649 options, effectively pushing customers toward pricier alternatives. Jio and Vodafone Idea are widely expected to make similar quiet adjustments over the coming weeks as part of the same run-up. Telecom analysts tracking the sector expect this to be the precursor to a broader, industry-wide tariff hike of **12% to 20%**, with the increase most likely landing between **late October and December** — deliberately timed to avoid the Dussehra and Diwali festive shopping season, when a visible price jump would draw the most public anger. Neither the central government nor telecom regulator **TRAI** is expected to step in, since tariff-setting is left to the operators.
key_points: Airtel has already **scrapped several popular prepaid plans**, including its ₹299 entry-level and ₹319, ₹579 and ₹649 packs.
Jio and Vodafone Idea are expected to make similar quiet moves in the coming weeks.
Analysts expect a **12-20% headline tariff hike** industry-wide, most likely between **late October and December**.
Operators are reportedly avoiding an explicit announcement until **after** the Dussehra-Diwali festive shopping season to dodge backlash.
The government and telecom regulator **TRAI are not expected to intervene** in the pricing decision.

depth.background: India's big three telecom operators — **Reliance Jio, Bharti Airtel and Vodafone Idea** — together serve over a billion mobile connections and have raised tariffs together in near-lockstep in past cycles, most recently in 2024. Jio in particular is under pressure to show stronger revenue growth ahead of a potential IPO, while Vodafone Idea has been financially fragile for years and badly needs higher average revenue per user to survive. Because switching your SIM is easy and cheap in India, operators typically raise prices together rather than one at a time, so as not to lose customers to a rival.

cards.title: Sensex and Nifty open flat and slip through the morning as costly oil and surging global bond yields keep pressuring Indian markets
cards.what_happened: The **BSE Sensex** opened almost flat at **77,218.05**, down about 17 points, while the **Nifty50** opened near **24,152**, down roughly 3 points. By mid-session (11:00 AM IST), the slide deepened: the Sensex was down **320.17 points (0.41%)** at **76,915.29**, and the Nifty50 fell **99.30 points (0.41%)** to **24,055.60**. Within the Sensex basket, **HCL Tech, Infosys, Eternal, Sun Pharma and Tech Mahindra** were the standout gainers, with HCL Tech up **1.22%**, even as the broader index slipped. On the primary market, newly-listed **Behari Lal Engineering** debuted at ₹465 on the NSE, a **63.16% premium** over its ₹285 issue price.
key_points: The **Sensex opened nearly flat** near 77,218 before sliding to a session low, down about **320 points (0.41%)** by mid-morning.
The **Nifty50 fell roughly 99 points (0.41%)** to trade near 24,056, extending pressure from **weak global cues**.
**IT stocks bucked the trend and rallied**, with **HCL Tech leading gainers**, up over 1%, along with Infosys, Eternal, Sun Pharma and Tech Mahindra.
The drag came from **renewed strength in crude oil prices** and a **sharp rise in global bond yields**, both raising costs for import-dependent India.
**Behari Lal Engineering listed with a 63% premium**, one of the day's bright spots on the primary market.

depth.background: Indian markets have been on edge this week as the fallout from the **Strait of Hormuz standoff** between the US and Iran keeps oil prices elevated, and as a sharp jump in **US Treasury yields** (partly tied to this week's Federal Reserve turmoil) makes it more expensive for India to borrow and pulls foreign money toward safer US assets. India imports roughly 85% of its crude oil, so global oil-price spikes hit it harder than most large economies, feeding into inflation and the trade deficit.

cards.title: ISRO to end its 7-month launch freeze in September with the GISAT-1A earth-imaging satellite
cards.what_happened: ISRO is set to return to the launch pad in the **first week of September** with **GISAT-1A (also called EOS-05)**, an earth-observation satellite designed for high-frequency imaging of large areas of India, launching aboard a **GSLV (Geosynchronous Satellite Launch Vehicle)**. This will be the agency's first launch since the **PSLV-C62 mission carrying EOS-N1 failed on January 12, 2026** — a gap of nearly **seven months**, one of ISRO's longest pauses between launches in recent memory. The announcement signals that ISRO's internal investigation into the January failure has concluded and its launch operations are being cleared to resume.
key_points: ISRO's next launch, the **GISAT-1A (EOS-05)** satellite, is targeted for the **first week of September** aboard a **GSLV rocket**.
It will be ISRO's **first launch since January 12**, when the **PSLV-C62/EOS-N1 mission failed**.
The gap is nearly **seven months** — one of the longest pauses between launches for ISRO in recent years.
GISAT-1A is built for **high-frequency imaging** of large areas of the Indian landmass, useful for disaster response and security monitoring.

depth.background: **ISRO (the Indian Space Research Organisation)** is India's national space agency, responsible for satellite launches, navigation, and space science. After a launch failure, agencies typically pause all missions to investigate the root cause before flying again — both to protect expensive payloads and to rebuild confidence in the rocket. ISRO's PSLV-C62 mission carrying the EOS-N1 satellite failed on **January 12, 2026**, triggering this extended freeze. GISAT-class satellites sit in geostationary orbit, letting them watch the same stretch of Indian territory continuously, unlike satellites that pass overhead only briefly.

cards.title: RBI abruptly closes its dollar-deposit swap window a month early, and bond yields jump
cards.what_happened: The Reserve Bank of India announced late last week that it would close the concessional FX swap facility for **FCNR(B) deposits on August 31**, a month earlier than the previously communicated September 30 end-date, citing an 'encouraging response' from banks. By August 13 the scheme had already drawn **$52.3 billion** in inflows, with banks expected to mobilise **$65-70 billion** in total once combined with other channels like overseas borrowing. The surprise move — coming just two weeks after the RBI governor had explicitly ruled out an early close — rattled bond traders. The **5-year government bond yield rose about 10 basis points** over two sessions to 6.44%, the **10-year yield climbed to 6.81%** from 6.76%, and the rupee slipped to **95.61 per dollar**. Banking stocks including HDFC, Axis, ICICI and SBI traded lower on the news.
key_points: The RBI shut its concessional **FCNR(B) dollar-swap window** on **August 31**, a month earlier than the originally planned **September 30** deadline.
The scheme had already pulled in **$52.3 billion** in inflows by August 13, prompting the early close.
The **5-year bond yield jumped ~10 basis points** over two sessions to 6.44%, and the **10-year yield rose to 6.81%** from 6.76%.
The rupee **weakened to 95.61 per dollar**, down 0.17% from the prior close.
RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra had **ruled out an early closure** just two weeks earlier at the August 5 policy meeting — surprising traders.

depth.background: Earlier this year the RBI launched a concessional swap scheme to encourage Indian banks to raise **FCNR(B) deposits** — dollar deposits from non-resident Indians that banks can swap for rupees with the central bank on favourable terms — as a way to shore up India's foreign-currency reserves and support the rupee. The scheme proved more successful than expected, drawing in tens of billions of dollars faster than the RBI anticipated. Just two weeks before this move, the RBI governor had told markets the scheme would run its full course to September 30.

cards.title: Bihar announces 32,388 new teacher vacancies — days after neighboring Jharkhand's exam system blew up
cards.what_happened: The BPSC released its official notification for **TRE 4.0**, advertising **32,388 vacancies** across primary, upper-primary, secondary, and senior-secondary teaching posts. Online registration opens **September 1** and closes **September 30** on the BPSC website, with the exam itself scheduled to run **September 22-27**. Eligible candidates must be between **18 and 37** years old and hold the relevant academic and teaching qualifications for the post they apply to.
key_points: The **Bihar Public Service Commission (BPSC)** released its TRE 4.0 notification for **32,388 teacher posts**.
Online applications open **September 1** and close **September 30**, with the exam scheduled for **September 22-27**.
Posts span **primary through senior secondary** school teachers; candidates aged **18-37** are eligible.
This is Bihar's **fourth** teacher recruitment exam (TRE) cycle since a 2023 push to fill mass teacher shortages.
It lands just as neighboring **Jharkhand** cancelled its own flagship recruitment exam over leak allegations.

depth.background: Bihar has run a series of large-scale **Teacher Recruitment Exams (TRE)** since 2023 to fill chronic teacher shortages in its government schools, hiring well over a hundred thousand teachers across the prior three cycles. Youth unemployment and the fairness of competitive government-job exams have become a major political flashpoint across India this year, most visibly in neighboring Jharkhand, where a cancelled exam and a 16-day hunger strike forced the state government to scrap an entire recruitment cycle over alleged irregularities.

As part of de-escalating the immediate confrontation, he called off a planned gherao of Chief Minister **Hemant Soren's** residence and a symbolic effigy-burning originally planned for August 20.

The shift from a single cancelled exam to a **permanent legal fix** raises the stakes for the Hemant Soren government.

That cancellation — a rare case of a state government reversing course under youth pressure — was itself the culmination of protests that included police lathi-charges and the detention of student leaders. **Devendra Mahto**, a leader of the Jharkhand Loktantrik Krantikari Morcha (JLKM), has emerged as the face of the movement.

Chandrasekaran** announced he will step down in **February**, meaning the group's board and trusts are simultaneously managing a leadership succession and this procedural stumble. cards.title: Jharkhand cancels a major recruitment exam after weeks of student protests and a 16-day hunger strike
cards.what_happened: On the night of **August 17-18**, Jharkhand's Cabinet, led by Chief Minister **Hemant Soren**, announced it was cancelling the JSSC-CGL exam and all other recruitment tests conducted by the private contractor **TDPL (TSR Data Processing Private Limited)**, and ordering an investigation. Shortly after midnight, protest leader **Mahto broke his 16-day hunger strike** at Ranchi's Sadar Hospital in front of state ministers Dipika Pandey Singh and Irfan Ansari; two other student leaders who had also been fasting, Umme Habiba and Rahul Kranti, ended their strikes too. The government's move came just ahead of an **August 18 deadline** protesters had set, warning that lakhs of students would march on the Chief Minister's house if demands weren't met. The cancellation, while a win for protesters demanding a clean process, creates a new problem: some candidates who **passed the exam legitimately** and have already started government jobs say the blanket cancellation is unfair to them, and may **challenge it in court**.

cards.title: Adani Enterprises becomes India's best Nifty 50 stock of 2026, up 34%, after a US court drops fraud charges
cards.what_happened: Adani Enterprises has climbed **34% so far in 2026**, reclaiming the position of the **best-performing stock on the Nifty 50** index. The rally accelerated after a **US federal judge permanently dismissed** the securities fraud charges that had been filed against Adani Group executives, closing out a legal overhang that dated back to 2024. Separately, global index provider **MSCI** raised the free-float factor — the share of a company's stock considered available for public trading — for several Adani group companies in its latest review, a technical change that forces passive index funds tracking MSCI benchmarks to buy more Adani stock. **Morgan Stanley** had already initiated coverage on the stock in June with an 'overweight' (buy) rating.
key_points: Adani Enterprises has risen **34% in 2026**, making it the **top-performing Nifty 50 stock** this year.
A **US federal judge permanently dismissed** the securities fraud case against Adani executives.
**MSCI** raised the free-float weighting of several Adani companies, forcing global index funds to buy more of the stock.
**Morgan Stanley** initiated coverage in June with an 'overweight' rating, backing further gains.
The rally marks a comeback from the **2023 Hindenburg report** that had wiped out over $150 billion in Adani Group value.

depth.background: Adani Enterprises, the flagship company of billionaire **Gautam Adani's** conglomerate, was at the center of India's biggest corporate governance storm in years after US short-seller **Hindenburg Research** accused the group of stock manipulation and accounting fraud in **2023**, erasing over $150 billion in market value at its worst point. The group was later hit with a **2024 US indictment** alleging a bribery scheme tied to solar energy contracts, which kept foreign investors wary and the stock under a cloud for nearly two years. Adani has consistently denied all wrongdoing.

cards.title: India's unemployment rate falls to 5.1% in July as more women join the workforce
cards.what_happened: Government PLFS data released this week showed India's unemployment rate for people aged 15 and above fell to **5.1% in July**, down from **5.5% in June**, marking one of the lowest readings in recent months. The improvement was led by rural India, where unemployment dropped to **4.5%** from 5%, while the urban rate held roughly steady at **6.7%**, barely changed from June's 6.6%. Alongside the falling unemployment rate, the **Labour Force Participation Rate** rose to **55.4%** from 54.4% the prior month, meaning a larger share of the working-age population is now either employed or actively job-hunting — with the data pointing to more women joining the workforce as a key driver.
key_points: India's unemployment rate dropped to **5.1% in July**, down from **5.5% in June**.
Rural unemployment fell more sharply, to **4.5%** from 5%, while urban unemployment stayed almost flat at **6.7%**.
The **Labour Force Participation Rate** — the share of people working or looking for work — rose to **55.4%** from 54.4%.
The improvement is driven partly by **more women entering the workforce**, according to the government data.
The figures come from the government's monthly **PLFS** jobs survey.

depth.background: India tracks employment through the **Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS)**, a monthly government survey that is the country's main official gauge of how many working-age people have jobs, are looking for jobs, or have dropped out of the job market entirely. A falling unemployment rate on its own can be misleading if it just means discouraged people stopped looking for work — economists watch it alongside the **Labour Force Participation Rate (LFPR)** to see whether more people are actually engaging with the job market, not fewer.

cards.title: A false rumor about a live wire triggers a deadly stampede at a Bihar temple, killing 7 devotees
cards.what_happened: On the **third Monday of Sawan**, a large crowd gathered at Bihar's Ashokdham Temple complex to offer prayers, swelling further after two trains dropped pilgrims between 6:30 and 6:45am. Around **6:45am**, an electric pole toppled near the men's queue, and a **rumor spread that a live wire had fallen** and that electric current was spreading through the crowd — though district officials later confirmed it was only a **cable wire**, not a live one. The panic pushed into the adjacent women's queue, and devotees began falling over one another in the crush. **At least seven women died** and several others were injured. Prime Minister Modi announced an ex-gratia payment of **₹2 lakh** from the PM's National Relief Fund for each victim's family and **₹50,000** for the injured, while the Bihar state government separately announced **₹4 lakh** per deceased.
key_points: **7 women devotees died** in a crush at the Ashokdham Temple in Bihar's Lakhisarai on the **third Monday of Sawan**.
An electric pole fell near the queue, sparking a **false rumor** that a live wire was spreading current through the crowd.
It was actually just a **cable wire**, but the panic sent devotees crashing into each other.
The crowd had swelled after **two trains** arrived within 15 minutes of the 6:45am incident.
PM Modi announced **₹2 lakh** ex-gratia per victim from PMNRF; Bihar added **₹4 lakh** more per family.

depth.background: **Sawan (Shravan)** is the holiest month of the year for worshippers of Shiva in North India, and its Mondays draw especially massive crowds to Shiva temples across the country. The **Ashokdham Temple** in Lakhisarai district, Bihar, is one such pilgrimage site, and stampedes at crowded Indian religious gatherings — driven less by malice than by poor crowd infrastructure and panic — are a recurring tragedy nationwide.

cards.title: 46 Manipur militants surrender arms as ex-CM says Amit Shah gave a 'positive response' on NRC-before-Census demand
cards.what_happened: Security forces in Manipur accepted the surrender of **46 cadres** belonging to the KCP-Taibanganba faction, a splinter of the banned Kangleipak Communist Party, who handed over their arms as part of the state's ongoing effort to wind down armed groups active during the ethnic conflict. Separately, former Chief Minister **N. Biren Singh** said Union Home Minister **Amit Shah** gave a "positive response" to his demand that the **National Register of Citizens (NRC)** be updated in Manipur before the next national **Census** goes ahead. The demand comes from the "Campaign for Just and Fair Delimitation" group, which called a two-day strike starting at midnight on August 17 to press the point, arguing that counting the population for the Census before verifying citizenship status would distort future seat delimitation and resource allocation in the state.
key_points: **46 cadres** of the banned KCP-Taibanganba faction surrendered with their weapons to security forces in Manipur
Former CM **N. Biren Singh** says Union Home Minister **Amit Shah** responded positively to demands for an NRC update before the Census
The demand is tied to a two-day strike called by the **"Campaign for Just and Fair Delimitation"** group, starting midnight August 17
Manipur has been gripped by ethnic conflict between the **Meitei and Kuki-Zo communities** since May 2023
The NRC-before-Census demand is politically explosive, since it would count residents by citizenship status before the next national headcount

depth.background: Manipur has been under a state of near-continuous ethnic conflict since May 2023, when clashes broke out between the majority **Meitei** community, concentrated in the Imphal Valley, and the **Kuki-Zo** tribal communities in the surrounding hills, over land rights, reserved-tribe status, and political representation. The violence killed hundreds and displaced tens of thousands, and the state was placed under President's Rule after N. Biren Singh resigned as Chief Minister earlier this year amid criticism of his handling of the crisis. Various armed groups — some claiming to represent one community or the other, others left over from decades-older insurgencies like the banned **Kangleipak Communist Party (KCP)** — have used the instability to operate in the hills, and the central government has periodically pushed peace talks and surrender-and-rehabilitation schemes to wind them down.

cards.title: Monsoon rainfall deficit hits 397 districts, threatening Ganga-belt paddy even as India's kharif sowing lags
cards.what_happened: New data shows that rainfall deficits are now affecting **397 districts** across India, with paddy-growing regions along the Ganga river belt — a traditional rice basket — facing **drought-like conditions**. While the cumulative seasonal rainfall deficit had narrowed to about **11.5% below the long-period average** by August 1 thanks to a partial monsoon recovery, the IMD is now forecasting **below-normal rainfall** for the remaining August-September stretch of the season, which would reverse some of that improvement. **Kharif sowing** acreage is running behind last year's pace, though the shortfall has narrowed considerably — from roughly 23% behind at the end of June to about 3% behind at the end of July, according to ratings agency ICRA — as farmers rushed to plant once rains picked up. Rice is seen as the most exposed crop, since paddy cultivation depends heavily on consistent monsoon water through the Ganga basin.
key_points: Rainfall shortfalls are now affecting **397 districts** across India, with paddy-growing areas along the Ganga facing **drought-like conditions**
The cumulative seasonal rainfall deficit had narrowed to about **11.5% below normal** by August 1, but the IMD forecasts **below-normal rain** for the rest of the season
**Kharif sowing** acreage is trailing last year, though the gap narrowed from roughly 23% behind at end-June to about 3% behind at end-July
**Paddy (rice)** is the crop most exposed, since it depends heavily on monsoon water in the Ganga basin's traditional growing belt
A weak kharif harvest would add pressure on food prices just as India's central bank is already watching inflation closely

depth.background: India's agricultural calendar runs on two main cropping seasons: **kharif**, sown with the June-to-September monsoon rains and harvested in autumn (rice, cotton, soybean, and other water-intensive crops), and **rabi**, the winter-sown season that relies more on irrigation. Because roughly half of India's farmland still isn't irrigated, the monsoon's timing and volume directly decide how much food gets grown and at what cost — a weak or late monsoon in any given year has historically pushed up food inflation and squeezed rural incomes. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) tracks rainfall against a **long-period average (LPA)**, and this year's monsoon started well below that average before a partial recovery in July narrowed the shortfall.

cards.title: Supreme Court tells the Centre to 'ground' airlines that ignore its airfare orders, as ticket-price complaints pile up
cards.what_happened: On **Monday, August 17**, a Supreme Court bench of **Justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta** directed the central government to **ground airlines** that fail to comply with the court's earlier directions on airfare pricing. The bench acted after petitioners alleged that airlines were simply **disregarding** the Centre's existing instructions on fare practices, with ticket prices for the same route varying wildly on the same day. In response, the Centre told the court that draft regulations governing **ticket pricing, surge fares, and excess baggage charges** have been fast-tracked and would be finalised within **three weeks**. The matter has been listed for its next hearing on **September 7**, when the court will check whether the promised rules have actually materialised.
key_points: A Supreme Court bench of **Justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta** told the Centre to **"ground" airlines** that don't comply with its directions on airfares
The court has been hearing a case over **unchecked, sharply rising ticket prices**, especially during festivals and peak travel
Petitioners told the court airlines are **ignoring the Centre's earlier directions** on fare transparency and surge pricing
The government said draft rules on **airfares, surge pricing, and baggage charges** have been fast-tracked and will be finalised within **three weeks**
The case returns to court on **September 7** to check on progress

depth.background: Indian air travelers have long complained about sharp, unpredictable spikes in ticket prices, particularly around festivals, long weekends, and other high-demand periods, with critics accusing airlines of exploiting limited competition. The Supreme Court has been hearing a public-interest case pushing the government to regulate this "surge pricing," and had earlier this year already flagged concern over exorbitant festival-season fares. This is the latest hearing in that ongoing case, with the court growing visibly impatient at the pace of government action.

cards.title: BJP unveils its new national team for the road to 2029 — Ram Madhav and Smriti Irani return, Piyush Goyal becomes treasurer
cards.what_happened: BJP national president **Nitin Nabin** announced a major overhaul of the party's central organisational team on **Monday, August 17**, naming 65 office-bearers of whom **51 are new**. Former Union minister **Smriti Irani** returns to a top party role as general secretary in charge of **Uttar Pradesh**, the country's most politically consequential state, which faces assembly elections in early 2027. Former RSS functionary **Ram Madhav** was named one of **13 national vice-presidents**, alongside veterans like former Rajasthan chief minister **Vasundhara Raje Scindia**. Union minister **Piyush Goyal** takes over as the party's treasurer, while **Amit Malviya**, the BJP's long-serving IT and social-media chief, was replaced by **Deepak Mhaske**. The reshuffled team includes 10 women and 6 leaders from minority communities, and party sources say it is explicitly designed with the 2029 general election and intervening state polls in mind.
key_points: BJP president **Nitin Nabin** announced a sweeping reshuffle of the party's national organisation on **Monday, August 17**
Of **65 office-bearers** named, **51 are new faces** — a major generational and factional reset
**Smriti Irani** returns as general secretary in charge of **Uttar Pradesh**, which votes in early 2027; **Ram Madhav** becomes a national vice-president
**Piyush Goyal** was named party treasurer, while IT/social-media chief **Amit Malviya** was dropped, replaced by **Deepak Mhaske**
The new team includes **13 vice-presidents**, **10 women** and **6 leaders from minority communities**

depth.background: India's ruling Bharatiya Janata Party periodically reshuffles its internal organisational leadership — separate from the government cabinet — to sharpen its election machinery ahead of major state and national polls. Nitin Nabin took over as party president earlier this year, and this reshuffle is his first major organisational overhaul, replacing much of the team built under his predecessor. Smriti Irani and Ram Madhav are both prominent leaders who had earlier been sidelined from top party roles, making their return notable; Uttar Pradesh, where Irani now takes charge, is India's most politically important state and goes to the polls in early 2027.

cards.title: IMD issues red alert for Odisha and Jharkhand as a Bengal depression brings heavy rain to 25 states
cards.what_happened: A **depression forming over the Bay of Bengal** has triggered the IMD's most serious warning level — a **red alert** — for parts of Odisha and Jharkhand, where isolated pockets could see more than **20 cm of rain in a single day**, enough to cause flash flooding. Hilly northern states — Jammu & Kashmir, Himachal Pradesh, and Uttarakhand — are under an **orange alert**, with forecasters warning heavy rain could trigger landslides, flash floods, and disruption to mountain roads. More broadly, the IMD has issued rain and thunderstorm warnings covering **25 states and Union Territories**, with wind gusts up to **65 kmph** in some areas. Delhi-NCR is expecting cloudy skies with light showers, while Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, West Bengal, and eastern Madhya Pradesh are all bracing for a heavier downpour.
key_points: The **India Meteorological Department (IMD)** issued a **red alert** for parts of Odisha and Jharkhand.
Isolated areas could see **over 20 cm of rainfall within 24 hours**.
An **orange alert** covers J&K, Himachal Pradesh, and Uttarakhand, warning of landslides and flash floods.
Heavy rain and thunderstorm warnings apply to **25 states and Union Territories**, with winds up to 65 kmph.
Delhi-NCR, UP, Bihar, West Bengal, and eastern Madhya Pradesh are all under some level of alert.

depth.background: India's monsoon (roughly June to September) brings the bulk of the country's annual rainfall, and it periodically intensifies into short, sharp 'depressions' — low-pressure weather systems over the Bay of Bengal that pull in moisture and dump it on land as they move inland. The IMD uses a four-colour alert system (green, yellow, orange, red) to flag how severe and how urgent a weather threat is, with red meaning 'take action' — the highest level, reserved for conditions expected to cause significant disruption or danger.

cards.title: Milky Mist Dairy shares jump 18% on debut, hit the upper circuit after a blockbuster IPO
cards.what_happened: Milky Mist Dairy Food debuted on India's stock exchanges on **August 18**, with shares opening at **Rs 165 apiece**, an 18% premium over its Rs 140 issue price. The stock extended gains after listing, hitting the **10% upper circuit at Rs 181.45** on the BSE. The Rs 1,553-crore public offer had drawn strong demand, closing **56.12 times subscribed** overall — bids came in for over 4.59 billion shares against roughly 818 million on offer. Qualified institutional buyers subscribed their portion 155.83 times, non-institutional investors 34.91 times, and retail investors 8.41 times. At its debut price, the company commands a market capitalization of about **Rs 12,702 crore**.
key_points: Milky Mist Dairy Food shares **listed at Rs 165**, an **18% premium** over the Rs 140 issue price, on both NSE and BSE.
The stock then hit its **10% upper circuit at Rs 181.45**, meaning trading was capped after gaining the maximum allowed for the day.
The **Rs 1,553-crore IPO** was subscribed **56 times over**, with bids for 4.59 billion shares against 818 million on offer.
Institutional investors led demand, subscribing their portion **155.8 times**, versus 34.9 times for non-institutional and 8.4 times for retail.
At the listing price, Milky Mist is valued at roughly **Rs 12,702 crore** (about $1.5 billion).

depth.background: Milky Mist is an Indian **packaged dairy and food company**, competing in a segment that includes players like Amul and Britannia as India's branded-food market grows with rising incomes and urbanization. An **IPO (initial public offering)** is when a private company sells shares to the public for the first time to raise money and list on a stock exchange; how eagerly investors bid for those shares — the **'subscription' level** — is a widely watched signal of market appetite. Strong dairy and consumer-staples IPOs have been relatively rare in a year when India's broader stock market has been volatile on global cues.

cards.title: Allahabad High Court slams UP government for taking Ram Mandir temple land without paying the agreed price
cards.what_happened: The **Allahabad High Court** ruled that the Uttar Pradesh government must deposit **Rs 1.21 crore, plus 8% annual interest**, as the unpaid balance owed for 1,512 square metres of temple land at Sugriv Kila in Ayodhya. A bench of **Justice Shekhar B. Saraf and Justice Abdhesh Kumar Chaudhary** heard the petition filed on behalf of the deity Shri Thakur Ram Janki Sugrivji Virajman Mandir. The court's order details that a **sale deed was executed on December 22, 2023**, valuing the land at Rs 1.38 crore — but the state took over the land for developing the Ram Janma Bhoomi Temple without paying that price. The bench criticized the government for a contradictory legal position: **acquiring the land under the 2023 sale deed while simultaneously arguing in court that the deity's title was invalid** and the land should never have been sold in the first place.
key_points: The court ordered UP to pay **Rs 1.21 crore plus 8% annual interest** for **1,512 sq metres** of land at Ayodhya's Sugriv Kila.
The land belongs to the deity **Shri Thakur Ram Janki Sugrivji**, taken over for developing the **Ram Janma Bhoomi Temple** complex.
A **sale deed was signed in December 2023** for Rs 1.38 crore, but the state never paid the agreed price, the court found.
Judges **Shekhar B. Saraf and Abdhesh Kumar Chaudhary** criticized the state for challenging the deity's ownership **while simultaneously taking the land.**
The order highlights a **legal contradiction**: the government questioned the temple's title to sell, even as it used that same sale deed to take possession.

depth.background: Ayodhya's Ram Mandir, consecrated after decades of legal and religious dispute culminating in a 2019 Supreme Court verdict, has driven a wave of **land acquisition** around the temple site for redevelopment — widened roads, a temple corridor, and related infrastructure. Landowners, including religious trusts and deities (which can legally hold property in India through a court-appointed manager), have separately been in disputes with the state over **fair compensation** for land taken for this expansion. This case involves land at 'Sugriv Kila,' tied to the deity Shri Thakur Ram Janki Sugrivji, represented in court as 'Virajman' — a legal status meaning the deity itself is treated as the petitioner.

cards.title: Sensex and Nifty slide as the Iran ceasefire lapses and oil jumps — why costlier crude hits India harder than most
cards.what_happened: Indian equity markets fell for a second straight session as the US-Iran ceasefire's expiry revived fears of prolonged Middle East conflict disrupting oil supply. The **Sensex slid 278 points to 77,451**, while the **Nifty 50 dropped 0.24% to 24,230**, extending losses from the previous close. **Brent crude pushed above $91 a barrel** and US crude (WTI) rose toward **$85**, both reflecting worry that fighting could threaten tanker traffic near the Strait of Hormuz, a key oil shipping route. IT stocks were hit hardest — the sector is especially exposed to global risk sentiment and a weaker rupee cuts both ways for exporters — with the **Nifty IT index down 1.24%** and heavyweights Infosys, TCS, HCLTech and Tech Mahindra all trading lower. The rupee weakened further and India's volatility index (India VIX) ticked up, both signs of rising investor nervousness.
key_points: The **Sensex fell 278 points** and the **Nifty 50 dropped below 24,250** in Tuesday trading as Middle East tensions spooked investors.
**Brent crude climbed above $91 a barrel** after the US-Iran ceasefire expired with no extension in sight, reviving fears that fighting could disrupt oil supply.
**IT stocks led the losses** — the Nifty IT index fell **1.24%**, with Infosys, TCS, HCLTech and Tech Mahindra all down — alongside a weaker rupee and rising global bond yields.
India imports the large majority of the crude oil it uses, so pricier oil directly threatens its import bill, inflation and corporate margins.

depth.background: India is one of the world's largest oil importers and buys the vast majority of the crude it consumes from abroad, so global oil-price swings hit its economy faster and harder than economies that produce more of their own energy. Indian stock indices — the **Sensex** (30 major companies on the Bombay Stock Exchange) and the **Nifty 50** (50 major companies on the National Stock Exchange) — are the two benchmarks used to gauge how Indian equity markets are doing overall. Oil-price spikes tend to hit India through multiple channels at once: a bigger import bill, a weaker rupee (since more dollars are needed to pay for oil), and higher inflation that can force the central bank to keep interest rates elevated.

cards.title: India's Gen-Z 'Cockroach' movement forced Modi's government to bend once — now Delhi is testing whether it can win young voters back
cards.what_happened: Protests spread nationwide after the exam-leak scandal, forcing the resignation of education minister Dharmendra Pradhan. The 'Cockroach Janta Party's' Instagram following ballooned past **25 million** — more than double the BJP's own following — turning a joke into a genuine youth political brand. In response, Modi released a string of casual, selfie-style Instagram videos addressing the exam leaks directly, and reportedly told cabinet colleagues that young people are 'just on Instagram,' pushing ministers to engage there with reels instead of traditional press conferences. In Uttar Pradesh, the BJP has launched a Gen Z outreach programme sending civil administration officers into schools for career counselling. But researchers tracking the movement say this is 'a battle for perception' — pointing out that no policy proposal so far actually changes the structural jobs shortage driving the anger, and online reaction to the BJP's reels-based outreach has often been skeptical or mocking.
key_points: The movement traces to India's **Chief Justice Surya Kant** comparing unemployed youth to 'cockroaches' — a jab that Gen Z turned into a badge of honor.
A leaked medical-entrance exam paper forced a **nationwide retest** and became the spark for mass protests over India's youth jobs crisis.
Education minister **Dharmendra Pradhan resigned** under pressure, and the satirical 'Cockroach Janta Party' now has over **25 million Instagram followers** — more than double the BJP's.
Modi has responded with **late-night Instagram reels** and reportedly told ministers to reach young people with reels, not press briefings.
Experts call it 'a battle for perception' rather than real policy change — no proposal so far fundamentally changes the underlying jobs shortage.

depth.background: India has the largest youth population of any country in the world, but secure, well-paying jobs are scarce relative to the number of young people competing for them — which is why ultra-competitive government and medical entrance exams became a flashpoint. In June, an Indian graduate student in Boston, Abhijeet Dipke, launched a satirical online 'Cockroach Janta Party' partly mocking Modi's BJP, riffing on the Chief Justice's remark. The movement stayed mostly online and ironic until a leaked medical entrance exam paper forced India's government to void results and order a retest, pushing years of pent-up frustration over the jobs crisis into the streets.

cards.title: India opens the BRICS Civil Forum in Delhi, the last major public event before it hosts the leaders' summit next month
cards.what_happened: Civil-society representatives from BRICS countries gathered in New Delhi for a two-day forum. Government officials framed India's chairship as guided by a **'people-centric and humanity-first' approach**, positioning the forum's recommendations to feed into the official 'sherpa track' — the working-level negotiations that produce the summit's final declaration. The forum caps off a year of preparatory meetings across Indian cities covering BRICS's three pillars: political and security cooperation, financial collaboration, and people-to-people partnership.
key_points: The **BRICS Civil Forum** is being held August 17-18 in New Delhi, gathering civil-society voices from BRICS nations.
MEA Economic Relations Secretary **Sudhakar Dalela** said the forum's inputs will feed into the **BRICS Leaders' Summit**.
India's 2026 chairship has already run **over 350 meetings** across Indian cities in the run-up to the summit.
The main event — the **18th BRICS Summit** — will be held in Delhi on **September 12-13, 2026**.
This year's chairship theme is **'Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability.'**

depth.background: **BRICS** is a bloc of major emerging economies — originally Brazil, Russia, India, China and South Africa, since expanded to include more members and partner countries (sometimes called 'BRICS Plus'). Each year a different member holds the rotating chairship and hosts the annual leaders' summit; India holds it in 2026 and will host the summit in its own capital for the first time since 2021.
