cards.title: Babar Azam ruled out of the Headingley Test with a hand injury — Salman Ali Agha steps in as Pakistan captain
cards.what_happened: Pakistan confirmed that **Babar Azam will not play the first Test** against England at Headingley after failing to recover from a right-hand injury. Babar was originally hit on the hand during Pakistan's Test series in the **West Indies** earlier this month, then took a further blow to the same hand from an **England Under-19 seamer** during a tour warm-up match at Beckenham. Head coach **Sarfaraz Ahmed** confirmed there is no fracture in the finger, but that Babar could not be cleared to play despite working through a brief net session. In his absence, **vice-captain Salman Ali Agha** will lead Pakistan for the opening Test, which began today. Pakistan's management indicated Babar's absence is for now confined to just this first Test of the three-match series.
key_points: **Babar Azam** has been ruled out of the **first Test against England** at Headingley with a **right-hand injury**.
**Salman Ali Agha** will captain Pakistan in Babar's place for the opening Test.
Babar was struck on the **same hand twice** — first against West Indies, then again in a **warm-up match at Beckenham** against an England Under-19 seamer.
Pakistan's team management says there's **no fracture**, and Babar's absence is, for now, **limited to this one Test**.
The injury comes just as **Joe Root** returns to the England captaincy for the first time since **2022**, making this a first Test both sides expected their comeback captains to lead.

thread.previously: As of yesterday, both Joe Root and Babar Azam were set to lead their sides in comeback roles at Headingley — Root returning to the England captaincy for the first time since giving it up in 2022, and Babar back in charge of a Pakistan side searching for direction.
thread.changed: Babar has now been ruled out of the first Test entirely. He never recovered from a right-hand injury sustained in a warm-up match at Beckenham — on top of an earlier blow to the same hand against West Indies — so vice-captain Salman Ali Agha will lead Pakistan instead when the match starts.

depth.background: Both England and Pakistan arrive at this three-Test series with captains making comebacks. Joe Root, one of England's greatest batters, gave up the England captaincy in 2022 after a difficult run and is now returning to lead the side for the first time since. Babar Azam, Pakistan's Test captain, has also been trying to steady a team that has struggled for consistency, arriving at Headingley on the back of Pakistan's first away Test win in three years. Babar had already been carrying a hand injury into the series after being struck during Pakistan's earlier tour of the West Indies.

cards.title: Two cricket teams in crisis, two comeback captains: Root and Babar collide today at Headingley
cards.what_happened: England and Pakistan begin a three-Test series today at **Headingley** in Leeds, with the first ball scheduled for **11:00am local time**. Joe Root captains England for the first time since relinquishing the role in 2022, while Babar Azam leads Pakistan back into a series after being restored as Test captain. Pakistan's build-up was clouded by uncertainty over Babar's fitness after he was struck on the right hand during a warm-up match in Kent, though he has been cleared to play. Both sides come in out of form — Pakistan sit eighth in the World Test Championship table with just two wins in six matches, while England, seventh, are coming off a 2-1 home series defeat to New Zealand.
key_points: **Joe Root** returns as England's full-time Test captain today, having given up the role back in **2022**.
**Babar Azam** leads Pakistan again after being reinstated, following a difficult run under predecessor **Shan Masood**.
Pakistan enter with an injury scare — Babar was **struck on the hand** during a Kent practice match before the series.
Both teams arrive under pressure: **England seventh, Pakistan eighth** in the current World Test Championship standings.
England open a new coaching era too, ending the **Bazball** period defined by Ben Stokes and Brendon McCullum.

depth.background: England's Test team spent the last several years under captain **Ben Stokes** and coach **Brendon McCullum**, playing an aggressive style nicknamed 'Bazball' that transformed the team's results and reputation. Stokes has since stepped back from Test captaincy, McCullum has moved to focus on England's white-ball teams, and Root — England's most experienced modern batter, who first captained the side from 2017 to 2022 — has taken the job back. Pakistan, meanwhile, have churned through captains, with **Babar Azam** now reinstated after Shan Masood's tenure produced a poor run of results, including 14 losses in their last 18 Tests.

cards.title: England hands its Test team to a foreign coach for the first time in the Bazball era — and it's not who Ben Stokes wanted
cards.what_happened: The England and Wales Cricket Board (ECB) has named **Stephen Fleming** as its new men's Test head coach on a four-year contract through September 2030, marking his first job coaching at international level despite a long, successful franchise-cricket coaching career. He replaces Brendon McCullum in the Test role specifically — McCullum remains in charge of England's white-ball teams — and arrives as Joe Root simultaneously takes back the Test captaincy he gave up in 2022. Fleming does have prior ties to English cricket, having previously played for Middlesex, Yorkshire, and Nottinghamshire (captaining Notts to a county title in 2005) and coached Southern Brave in The Hundred.
key_points: **Stephen Fleming**, the former New Zealand captain and longtime Chennai Super Kings coach, is England's new men's Test head coach.
He signed a **four-year deal** with the ECB running through **September 2030** — his first-ever international coaching job.
He replaces **Brendon McCullum**, who stepped down from the Test role after England's series loss to New Zealand in June but stays on to run England's white-ball teams.
The appointment comes as **Joe Root** simultaneously returns as full-time Test captain.
It's a pointed twist: former captain **Ben Stokes** recently said he'd like the England head coach job **one day** — it just went to someone else, now.

depth.background: England's Test side has been coached by fellow New Zealander Brendon McCullum since 2022, alongside captain Ben Stokes, in a partnership that produced the aggressive 'Bazball' era and transformed the team's results and public profile. That era effectively ended when Stokes stepped back from the Test captaincy and McCullum, after a home series defeat to New Zealand in June, chose to step down from the Test coaching role specifically while remaining in charge of England's white-ball (ODI and T20) sides. **Stephen Fleming** built his post-playing reputation primarily in franchise cricket, most notably as the long-serving head coach of the Chennai Super Kings in the IPL, rather than in international coaching.

cards.title: Rishabh Pant returns to Delhi Capitals in a blockbuster swap that sends Kuldeep Yadav to Lucknow
cards.what_happened: Delhi Capitals and Lucknow Super Giants **officially completed a trade** ahead of IPL 2027: **Rishabh Pant returns to Delhi Capitals**, the team he represented for nine seasons and 111 matches (2016-2024, the most appearances by any player in DC's history), while **Kuldeep Yadav moves to Lucknow Super Giants** after five seasons and 72 wickets in 65 matches for Delhi. On the financial side, Pant rejoins DC at a **revised fee of ₹15 crore**, down sharply from the **₹27 crore** LSG paid to sign him in the 2025 mega auction. Kuldeep moves at his **existing ₹13.5 crore fee**. The fee gap means **LSG gains roughly ₹13.5 crore** in extra purse space for the next auction, while **DC's purse is reduced by ₹1.5 crore**.
key_points: **Rishabh Pant** is heading back to **Delhi Capitals**, the franchise he played nine seasons for, in a trade with Lucknow Super Giants.
**Kuldeep Yadav** moves the other way to **Lucknow Super Giants**, after five seasons taking 72 wickets for Delhi.
Pant rejoins DC at a **cut fee of ₹15 crore**, down from the **₹27 crore** LSG paid for him in the 2025 mega auction — roughly a **44% pay cut**.
Kuldeep moves at his existing **₹13.5 crore** fee, leaving LSG with **~₹13.5 crore extra** in their purse for the next auction, while DC loses ₹1.5 crore from theirs.
Pant made **111 appearances for Delhi** from 2016-2024, the most of any player in the franchise's history.

depth.background: The IPL (Indian Premier League) allows franchises to **trade contracted players** between seasons, subject to negotiated fees that adjust each team's remaining auction budget ('purse'). Rishabh Pant, one of India's most recognizable wicketkeeper-batters, spent nearly a decade as the face of Delhi Capitals before a big-money move to Lucknow Super Giants in the 2025 mega auction. Kuldeep Yadav, a left-arm wrist-spin bowler, had been one of Delhi's most effective bowlers over five seasons. This trade effectively **reunites Pant with his old franchise** while Delhi gives up a key bowler to make it happen.

cards.title: Keith Barker retires at 39 after a knee injury cuts short his comeback season at Warwickshire
cards.what_happened: Keith Barker has announced his retirement from professional cricket after a **17-season career**, ending a comeback stint at **Warwickshire** — the county where he made his name — that was cut short by a persistent **knee complaint**. Across ten seasons at Edgbaston (2009-2018) he took **357 wickets** and scored **six first-class centuries**, and was part of the side that won the **2012 County Championship**. After moving to Hampshire for the 2019 season, he added a further **191 wickets and 1,975 runs**, cementing his reputation as one of county cricket's most dependable all-rounders.
key_points: Left-arm all-rounder **Keith Barker** has retired from professional cricket after a **17-season career**.
He returned to **Warwickshire** this summer at age 39 hoping for one more good year.
A persistent **knee complaint** forced the decision, cutting the comeback short.
At Edgbaston alone (2009-2018) he took **357 wickets** and scored **six centuries**, helping win the **2012 County Championship**.
At Hampshire (from 2019) he added **191 more wickets** and nearly **2,000 runs**.

depth.background: **Keith Barker** spent a decade at **Warwickshire** (2009-2018), becoming one of the county's most reliable all-rounders and helping the club win the **County Championship title in 2012**. He then moved to **Hampshire** ahead of the 2019 season, continuing to perform as a genuine batting-and-bowling all-rounder. This year, at 39, he rejoined Warwickshire on a short-term deal for one more season.

cards.title: BCCI expands anti-corruption monitoring to every state T20 league after a TNPL player smuggled in an undeclared phone
cards.what_happened: The BCCI announced it is expanding **ACSU anti-corruption monitoring to cover every match in every state-run T20 league**, a first for the board, after detecting a rise in unauthorized approaches to players, franchise owners and team officials by suspected bookmakers. The immediate trigger was an incident in the **Tamil Nadu Premier League (TNPL)**, where a player was fined **₹1 lakh** and suspended after being caught carrying an undeclared mobile phone into the restricted players' area — a rule breach because unmonitored phones are one of the easiest ways for a player to be contacted or to pass on information during a match. BCCI secretary **Devajit Saikia** publicly backed a zero-tolerance approach, saying even a relatively minor breach like undeclared phone possession would now draw firm action, framing it as part of a broader effort to close gaps bookmakers could exploit across the many state leagues that have sprung up in recent years.
key_points: BCCI's **Anti-Corruption and Security Unit (ACSU)** will now cover **every match** in state-run T20 leagues, not just marquee tournaments
The trigger: a **Tamil Nadu Premier League (TNPL)** player was fined **₹1 lakh** and suspended for carrying an undeclared phone into the restricted players' area
BCCI has detected a **rise in unauthorized approaches** to players, owners and officials by suspected bookmakers across state leagues
BCCI secretary **Devajit Saikia** is publicly pushing a **zero-tolerance stance**, even for minor breaches like phone possession
State T20 leagues have multiplied across India in recent years, creating far more matches for corruption units to realistically police

depth.background: India's **state T20 leagues** — like the Tamil Nadu Premier League (TNPL), Karnataka Premier League, and similar tournaments in other states — have multiplied over the past decade as a lower-tier, franchise-style feeder circuit below the IPL, giving domestic players exposure and a bit of extra income. Because these leagues involve far more matches, smaller budgets, and less scrutiny than the IPL, they've long been seen as a softer target for match-fixing approaches by bookmakers, who typically try to recruit less-well-paid or less-experienced players. The BCCI's **Anti-Corruption and Security Unit (ACSU)** exists to police exactly this kind of risk — restricting player phone access during matches, monitoring betting patterns, and investigating approaches — but has historically concentrated its heaviest resources on the IPL rather than the many state leagues.

cards.title: ICC fines two Pakistan pacers for send-off celebrations in their World Test Championship opener
cards.what_happened: The **ICC** sanctioned Pakistan fast bowlers **Khurram Shahzad** and **Mohammad Abbas** for breaching Level 1 of its Code of Conduct during the **opening Test** of the current **World Test Championship** cycle against the **West Indies**. The charges relate to on-field celebrations, words, or gestures directed at batters after dismissing them, which match officials judged to be insulting, provocative, or likely to provoke an aggressive response. As a Level 1 breach, the sanctions are expected to be limited to reprimands and/or fines rather than any playing suspension.
key_points: Pakistan bowlers **Khurram Shahzad** and **Mohammad Abbas** were sanctioned by the **ICC**.
The breach came during the **opening Test** of the new World Test Championship cycle against the **West Indies**.
Both were found to have breached **Level 1** of the ICC's Code of Conduct.
The charge relates to on-field words or gestures toward dismissed batters judged **insulting or provocative**.
Level 1 breaches typically carry a **reprimand and/or a fine**, not a playing ban.

depth.background: Cricket's global governing body, the **ICC**, enforces a tiered Code of Conduct to police player behavior on the field. **Level 1** is the mildest tier, covering things like excessive celebrating after a wicket in a way that targets or provokes the dismissed batter — common in fast-bowling send-offs, where a bowler reacts aggressively toward a batter they've just dismissed. Punishments escalate through the levels, with the most serious breaches carrying match bans.

cards.title: Pakistan is set to drop Shaheen Afridi from Tests over workload — so he's out playing domestic cricket instead
cards.what_happened: Pakistan's selectors are reportedly set to leave **Shaheen Shah Afridi** out of the Test squads for the team's upcoming tours of the **West Indies and England**, citing the need to manage his workload across a packed international schedule. Afridi is said to be unhappy with the decision. In the meantime, rather than being rested outright, Afridi has been playing in Pakistan's domestic **National Champions Cup**, where his team, Sparco Paints Pakistan Gold, beat UOL Pakistan Whites by five wickets on **August 16** to reach the tournament final — Afridi himself took **3 wickets for 26 runs** in the match. Alongside him, fellow pacers **Naseem Shah** and **Hasan Ali**, and veteran spinner **Noman Ali**, are also reportedly being moved out of the Test line-up as part of a wider shake-up of Pakistan's red-ball attack.
key_points: Shaheen Shah Afridi is likely to be **left out of Pakistan's Test squads** for the West Indies and England tours.
The stated reason is **workload management** — but Afridi is reportedly **unhappy** about the decision.
While the squad call plays out, Afridi has been turning out in Pakistan's **National Champions Cup** domestic tournament.
His side reached the final on August 16 with Afridi taking **3 wickets for 26 runs**.
Fellow pacers **Naseem Shah** and **Hasan Ali**, plus spinner **Noman Ali**, are also reportedly being eased out of the Test set-up.

depth.background: **Shaheen Shah Afridi** is Pakistan's premier fast bowler and a former Test vice-captain, central to the team's red-ball attack for years. Cricket boards increasingly rotate and rest fast bowlers across a packed international calendar to protect them from injury and burnout, a practice known as **workload management** — but the players on the receiving end don't always agree with the timing or the selectors' reasoning, and disputes over who gets rested can become selection flashpoints.

cards.title: Jemimah Rodrigues ruled out of the Women's Asia Cup and Asian Games with a hamstring tear — Pratika Rawal steps in
cards.what_happened: Rodrigues **tore her right hamstring** — described as a 'high-grade' tear, the more serious end of the injury scale — while playing for Southern Brave in The Hundred on **August 3**. After medical assessment, India's Women's Selection Committee ruled her out of both the upcoming **Women's Asia Cup**, which runs from **August 28 to September 13** in Dubai, and the **Asian Games** later this year. **Pratika Rawal**, who has previously played Test cricket for India, has been named as her replacement, earning a recall to the white-ball squad. The rest of the squad remains largely settled around captain **Harmanpreet Kaur** and vice-captain **Smriti Mandhana**.
key_points: Rodrigues suffered a **high-grade right hamstring tear** playing for Southern Brave in **The Hundred** on August 3.
She is ruled out of both the **Women's Asia Cup (Aug 28–Sep 13)** and the **Asian Games**.
**Pratika Rawal** has been named her replacement, earning a recall to the squad.
**Harmanpreet Kaur** continues as captain with **Smriti Mandhana** as vice-captain.
It's the second major batting reshuffle in the squad, after 18-year-old **G. Kamalini** was added as second wicketkeeper.

depth.background: Jemimah Rodrigues is one of India's most important middle-order batters in white-ball cricket and had been named in India's squad for the **Women's Asia Cup 2026** in the UAE, a tournament India has dominated with seven titles historically. She'd been playing in **The Hundred**, England's short-format franchise league, for Southern Brave — a common pre-tournament tune-up for international players — when she picked up the injury.

prev_ref.title: Australia's selectors weigh batting changes after a 'Darwin disaster' loss to Bangladesh, as photos of players golfing spark backlash

cards.title: Australia axes Jake Weatherald after the 'Darwin disaster', recalls Matt Renshaw — and gives Marnus Labuschagne one more Test to save his spot
cards.what_happened: Following the nine-wicket loss to Bangladesh in Darwin — Australia's first-ever Test defeat to Bangladesh — national selectors dropped opening batter Jake Weatherald, who scored 23 and 0 in the match, and recalled Matt Renshaw for the second Test in Mackay. Marnus Labuschagne, who managed only 1 and 31 at No.3, keeps his place in the squad, but head coach Andrew McDonald publicly acknowledged the right-hander has work to do to hold his spot going forward. The fallout from the Darwin loss was compounded by photos of players golfing during the post-match period, which drew criticism from fans and commentators questioning the squad's focus.

cards.title: Bangladesh's historic Test win over Australia gets a phone call from the PM — and a Cabinet shout-out
cards.what_happened: Bangladesh beat Australia by nine wickets in the first Test at Marrara Cricket Ground in Darwin, chasing down their target in just 14.2 overs for the loss of one wicket (Tanzid Hasan Tamim). Off-spinner **Mehidy Hasan Miraz** took a five-wicket haul on the fourth day to help bowl Australia out for 284 in their second innings, setting up the small final chase. The win makes Bangladesh only the **third Asian team**, after India and Pakistan, to beat Australia in a Test match on Australian soil — a genuinely historic milestone for a team that had never managed it before. Bangladesh's Prime Minister **Tarique Rahman** personally called BCB (Bangladesh Cricket Board) director Fahim Sinha to congratulate the team, and the Bangladeshi Cabinet formally congratulated the national cricket team at its weekly meeting held today, August 17 — an unusually prominent political response to a cricket result.
key_points: Bangladesh beat Australia by **nine wickets** in Darwin — only the **third Asian team ever**, after India and Pakistan, to win a Test on Australian soil.

The win lands amid a tense political backdrop, with Bangladesh's interim leadership navigating a difficult post-Hasina transition and friction with India over cricket and diplomacy.

depth.background: Bangladesh's national cricket team, nicknamed the **Tigers**, has historically struggled overseas against the strongest Test nations, and had never before won a Test match in Australia — one of the hardest places in the world to win, thanks to bouncy, fast pitches suited to Australia's traditionally strong pace attacks. Bangladesh itself has been through a turbulent political transition since 2024, and cricket has increasingly become entangled with politics there: the country's relationship with India, in particular, has been strained by the ongoing standoff over extraditing former PM Sheikh Hasina, spilling over into sports diplomacy and scheduling disputes. A prime minister personally calling to congratulate a cricket team, and a full Cabinet formally noting a sports result, signals how much national pride is riding on cricket success right now as a rare unifying moment.

cards.title: Ravindra Jadeja joins cricket's most exclusive all-rounder club — only the 4th player ever to reach 4,000 runs and 350 wickets
cards.what_happened: On **Day 3 of the Galle Test** against Sri Lanka (August 17), Ravindra Jadeja picked up his 350th Test wicket, making him the **first Indian left-arm bowler** to reach that mark — with the next-best Indian left-armer, Zaheer Khan, a distant second on 311. Combined with his batting tally, Jadeja simultaneously became the **4th player in the history of Test cricket** to record both 4,000 runs and 350 wickets, joining Kapil Dev (5,248 runs, 434 wickets), Ian Botham (5,200 runs, 383 wickets) and Daniel Vettori (4,531 runs, 362 wickets). He reached the milestone in his **90th Test**, the second-fastest of the four to do so, behind only Botham's 83 matches. He is also now the 5th Indian bowler overall past 350 Test wickets, joining Anil Kumble (619), Ravichandran Ashwin (537), Kapil Dev (434) and Harbhajan Singh (417). The feat came fittingly in **India's 600th-ever Test match**.
key_points: Jadeja became the **first Indian left-arm bowler** to reach 350 Test wickets, during Day 3 in Galle.

depth.background: Ravindra Jadeja, now **37**, debuted for India in 2012 and spent years being underestimated as 'just' a containing bowler and lower-order hitter, even as his numbers quietly piled up across more than a decade. The exclusive club of Test all-rounders who've reached both **4,000 runs and 350 wickets** includes some of the sport's greatest names — England's Ian Botham, South Africa/New Zealand great Daniel Vettori, and India's own Kapil Dev, long considered the gold standard of Indian all-round cricket. Reaching that double is rare because it demands both **longevity** (staying fit and selected for well over a decade) and genuine two-way excellence, not just being good at one skill.

cards.title: Gavaskar demands the BCCI make IPL trade fees public, as Hardik Pandya trade talk builds
cards.what_happened: Former India captain **Sunil Gavaskar** publicly called on the BCCI to make IPL trade financial details fully transparent, arguing that keeping the numbers confidential leaves other franchises unable to verify whether a trade complies with the league's salary cap. 'It's important for full transparency,' Gavaskar said, adding that the IPL is 'the greatest T20 league in the world' and needs to guard against 'finger-pointing... from those jealous of it.' The comments follow the completed trade sending **Rishabh Pant** back to Delhi Capitals and **Kuldeep Yadav** to Lucknow Super Giants, and come as speculation builds over a possible trade involving Mumbai Indians all-rounder **Hardik Pandya**, with both **Kolkata Knight Riders** and **Rajasthan Royals** reported to have made informal approaches to Mumbai Indians — though nothing has been finalised or made public.

depth.background: The **IPL (Indian Premier League)** allows franchises to trade contracted players between each other's rosters for an agreed fee, on top of the annual player auction. Because the league operates under a hard **salary cap** — a maximum total amount each team can spend on player salaries — the actual money changing hands in a trade matters: it affects how much cap space each side has left. Currently the BCCI, the two clubs involved, and the player know the exact trade figure, but it is not published, unlike the player-movement itself, which is announced publicly. Gavaskar's comments come after the **Rishabh Pant–Kuldeep Yadav** trade, where Pant moved to Delhi Capitals at a reported ₹15 crore (about $1.8 million) fee and Kuldeep Yadav went to Lucknow Super Giants for roughly ₹13.5 crore.

cards.title: India vice-captain KL Rahul forced off with severe cramps in Galle — a fitness scare that revives India's rotation worries

depth.background: Ben Stokes stepped back from the England Test captaincy, reopening the question of who leads the side. Root had previously held the England Test captaincy for years before Stokes took over, giving him deep leadership experience but also raising questions about workload given how long and demanding the England captaincy has historically been.

cards.title: India push past 460 on a rain-hit Day 2 in Galle as Padikkal falls for 167 and Jurel chips in a fifty
cards.what_happened: Resuming from Day 1's strong position, India extended their innings through a rain-interrupted Day 2, with **Devdutt Padikkal** carrying on from his overnight century to reach **167** before finally being dismissed. Lower-order contributions, including a fighting fifty from **Dhruv Jurel**, helped India push their total past the 450-run mark, and the side closed the day on **460 for 9**. Persistent rain forced repeated delays and a shortened day's play, adding an extra layer of difficulty for both sides in managing the conditions. The innings has given India a commanding position heading into the remaining days of the Test, which also holds special significance as India's **600th Test match**.

**Devdutt Padikkal** extended his overnight century to **167** before being dismissed, converting Day 1's platform into a big personal score.
**Dhruv Jurel** chipped in with a fighting **fifty** lower down the order to help India push past 450.
This is India's historic **600th Test match**, a landmark reached by very few teams in the sport's history.

cards.title: BCCI and its own selectors are at war over Rohit Sharma's ODI future
cards.what_happened: According to multiple Indian reports, the **Agarkar-led selection panel** privately told Rohit on **two separate occasions** — right after this year's IPL, and again ahead of India's ODI series in England — that the team was moving past him for the 2027 World Cup cycle. Rohit responded on the field with a **138 off 110 balls at Lord's**, one of his best knocks in years, which reignited public support for him. Days later, **BCCI secretary Devajit Saikia** told the press Rohit "will continue to represent the country as long as he is in the scheme of things" — a statement selectors saw as **publicly overruling their private call**. Reports now say the BCCI has asked selectors to assess Rohit **series-by-series** rather than make a hard cutoff, and that he is now **in line to be picked for India's home ODI series against West Indies** in late September. Agarkar himself completes **three years as chief selector this September** and is up for a one-year extension, with the board reportedly set to discuss his future once the ongoing India-Sri Lanka Test series ends — timing that puts his tenure squarely inside this row.
key_points: Selectors reportedly told **Rohit Sharma twice** — after the IPL and again before the England ODIs — that his **2027 World Cup** plans didn't include him
Rohit answered with **138 off 110 balls** at Lord's during the England series
BCCI secretary **Devajit Saikia** publicly said Rohit stays 'as long as he is in the scheme of things', contradicting the selectors
Some selectors feel **'betrayed'**, believing the board caved to social-media pressure, not form
Chief selector **Ajit Agarkar's** own contract extension talks are now tangled up in the fallout

depth.background: **Ajit Agarkar**, India's chief selector since 2023, leads a panel working with head coach **Gautam Gambhir** to build a younger squad — centred on players like **Yashasvi Jaiswal** — for the 2027 ODI World Cup in South Africa. **Rohit Sharma**, 39, is India's ODI captain and one of the format's greatest openers, but his 50-over workload has been under selector scrutiny for over a year. The **BCCI's administrative wing** (secretary Devajit Saikia and the office bearers) sits above the cricket-only selection committee, and normally the two operate in lockstep in public.

cards.title: Pakistan drop veteran pacer Diana Baig from both Asia Cup and Asian Games squads

Fatima Sana was confirmed as captain of both sides. Baig, a long-time first-choice pacer, did not make either squad — unusually, she was **not even named as a reserve/standby player**, a status normally reserved for players still in selectors' plans. Veteran all-rounder Aliya Riaz was also left out of the Asia Cup squad, though named for the Asian Games. The Asia Cup squad leans toward younger and uncapped players such as Eyman Fatima and Umm-e-Hani. The tournament itself is a high-stakes one: Pakistan open against Thailand on September 1 before a marquee clash with India on September 5 in Dubai.

Diana Baig left out of **both** squads and not even named among reserves

depth.background: Diana Baig is a Pakistan cricket fixture: she is the **first international cricketer, male or female, from Gilgit-Baltistan**, and even played international football for Pakistan before focusing fully on cricket after 2015. A right-arm medium-fast bowler, she made her Pakistan debut in **2015** and has since been one of the team's most reliable pace options across multiple World Cups. Fatima Sana, the regular captain, had briefly missed white-ball games on Pakistan's Sri Lanka tour to fulfil a contract with Birmingham Phoenix in the Hundred, but is now back leading both squads.

cards.title: Suryakumar Yadav trade buzz builds: reports link MI star to KKR in a possible Shreyas Iyer swap

Yadav's underwhelming IPL 2026 season, in which Mumbai Indians missed the playoffs, has added weight to the talk that the franchise may be open to moving him on. One version of the deal reportedly sends **Shreyas Iyer** to MI in return
Comes months after Yadav was **stripped of India's T20I captaincy**, replaced by Iyer
Yadav managed only around **200 runs** across IPL 2026 as MI missed the playoffs
**No official confirmation** yet from MI, KKR, or Yadav himself

cards.title: Bangladesh beat Australia by 9 wickets in Darwin — their first-ever Test win on Australian soil
cards.what_happened: Bangladesh posted 426 in their first innings, built around **Tanzid Hasan's** maiden Test century — the first century by a Bangladeshi batter in a Test on Australian soil. Australia collapsed to 198 all out in reply, with Hasan Mahmud taking a career-best 6/55, forcing Bangladesh to enforce the follow-on. Australia's second innings put up more resistance, with Cameron Green making a fighting century (his highest Test score in Australia) and the total reaching 284 all out, with Mehidy Hasan Miraz taking a five-wicket haul. That left Bangladesh needing just 57 to win, which they chased down for the loss of no wickets in the second session of day four — Mominul Haque hit the winning runs, finishing 30 not out alongside Shadman Islam's unbeaten 25. Hasan Mahmud's match figures of 9/111 were described by wire reports as the best by a visiting bowler in Australia not named Jasprit Bumrah in the past 15 years, and he was named Player of the Match.
key_points: Bangladesh chased down a target of just **57** to win by **9 wickets**, completing a historic first-ever Test victory on Australian soil.
**Hasan Mahmud** took match figures of **9/111**, including a career-best 6/55, and was named Player of the Match.
Australia followed on and were bowled out for **284** despite **Cameron Green's century**, after Bangladesh posted **426** in their first innings.
It's Bangladesh's **first Test series appearance in Australia since 2003**, when the hosts swept 2-0.
Wires are calling it one of the **biggest upsets in Test cricket history**, days after Bangladesh had been bowled out for just 54 in a warm-up match.

depth.background: Bangladesh have played Test cricket for over two decades but had never previously won a Test match in Australia, and hadn't toured there for a Test series since 2003, when Australia won 2-0. Going into this match at Marrara Oval in Darwin, expectations were low — Bangladesh had been bowled out for just 54 by a Cricket Australia XI in their tour warm-up game just before the series.

cards.title: Cricket Australia's chief backs cutting back 'meaningless' bilateral ODIs — but warns of a revenue hit
cards.what_happened: Speaking in Darwin during Australia's Test against Bangladesh, Cricket Australia chief executive Todd Greenberg said he agrees that international matches 'need to matter and have context and jeopardy,' adding: 'Creating jeopardy and meaning into the games we play is important.' His comments echo remarks made earlier in the week by ICC chief executive Sanjog Gupta, who said the era of 'randomly scheduled' bilateral series 'has to come to an end,' while arguing the ODI format can survive if it's tied more closely to the ODI World Cup. Greenberg noted Gupta had made similar comments directly to Cricket Australia staff during a recent visit to Melbourne. But Greenberg also flagged a real concern: bilateral ODIs currently make up a significant share of Cricket Australia's broadcast-rights revenue, so stripping them out entirely would have a commercial cost. Greenberg is a member of the ICC working group currently finalizing the Future Tours Programme — the internationally agreed cricket schedule — for 2028-31, and the group is also sketching an early, rough version of the following 2032-35 cycle.
key_points: Cricket Australia CEO **Todd Greenberg** says international cricket needs more **'jeopardy and meaning'**, backing a rethink of routine bilateral ODI series.
His comments echo **ICC CEO Sanjog Gupta**, who says the era of 'randomly scheduled' bilateral series 'has to come to an end'.
Greenberg flagged a real tension: bilateral ODIs make up a **significant share of Cricket Australia's broadcast revenue**.
Greenberg sits on the **ICC working group** now finalizing the international schedule for **2028-31**, and sketching an early draft for 2032-35.

depth.background: One-Day Internationals (ODIs) — 50-overs-a-side matches — sit between Test cricket's prestige and T20's popularity and money, and have increasingly been criticized as filler content when played as routine bilateral series between two countries outside a World Cup. Administrators, including the ICC's own CEO, have been signaling a shift toward tying ODIs more tightly to context that matters, like World Cup qualification, rather than filling the calendar with series that carry little stake.

cards.title: Bangladesh close in on a historic first-ever Test win on Australian soil as hosts slump to 161/4, still 67 runs behind
cards.what_happened: Australia's second innings stumbled to **161 for 4 at stumps on day four**, still **67 runs behind** Bangladesh's commanding first-innings total. All-rounder **Cameron Green** (43 not out off 86 balls) and wicketkeeper **Alex Carey** (19 not out off 50 balls) are the recognized batters left at the crease, carrying what's left of Australia's hopes of saving or winning the match. Bangladesh's bowlers have kept chipping away at Australia's top order throughout the innings, and with only a handful of recognized batters left, Bangladesh need just **six more wickets** to complete what would be their **first-ever Test win on Australian soil** — and arguably the biggest victory in Bangladesh's Test cricket history. The match, the first of the series, continues into a fifth and potentially deciding day at Darwin's Marrara Stadium.
key_points: Australia closed day four on **161 for 4**, still trailing Bangladesh by **67 runs**.
Cameron Green (**43 not out**) and Alex Carey (19 not out) are the hosts' last recognized batting pair.
Bangladesh's first innings total of **426** was built on Mehidy Hasan Miraz's 65, with Josh Hazlewood taking 6-89 in reply.

depth.background: **Bangladesh have never won a Test match in Australia**, in any of their previous tours, making this first Test of their 2026 series a genuine shot at cricketing history. The match is being played in **Darwin**, a less common Australian Test venue whose tropical conditions differ from Australia's traditional Test grounds. Bangladesh batted first and posted a commanding **426 all out**, anchored by Mehidy Hasan Miraz's 65, before Australia's reply collapsed to **198 all out** in their first innings, with fast bowler **Josh Hazlewood taking 6 wickets for 89 runs**. cards.title: The Hundred sets its Lord's finals: Manchester Super Giants and Sunrisers Leeds join Trent Rockets
cards.what_happened: **Manchester Super Giants** defeated **Sunrisers Leeds** by 20 runs in Friday's men's Eliminator at the Kia Oval, setting up a men's final against table-toppers **Trent Rockets** at Lord's. In the women's competition, played the same day, **Sunrisers Leeds** beat **Southern Brave** by five wickets — Lauren Winfield-Hill (37) and Deepti Sharma (28 not out) guiding them home with 11 balls to spare after Southern Brave posted 114/7 — to reach the women's final, also against Trent Rockets. Both finals will be played at **Lord's on Sunday, August 16**, with the women's final at 2:15pm and the men's at 6pm; a reserve day is scheduled for Monday, August 17 in case of a washout. Trent Rockets finished top of both the men's and women's points tables this season, meaning they avoided the Eliminator entirely and go into Sunday's finals with extra rest compared to their opponents.
key_points: **Manchester Super Giants** beat Sunrisers Leeds by **20 runs** in the men's Eliminator at the Kia Oval to book a Lord's final spot against **Trent Rockets**, who topped the table.
In the women's competition, **Sunrisers Leeds** won a tense **five-wicket** Eliminator over Southern Brave to reach their final, also against **Trent Rockets**.
Both finals are at **Lord's on Sunday, August 16** — women's at 2:15pm, men's at 6pm — with a reserve day on Monday if needed.
**Trent Rockets** finished top of both the men's and women's tables this season, earning a rest before the final while their rivals fought through the Eliminator.
The Hundred is now in its **sixth year** as English cricket's short-format franchise competition.

depth.background: **The Hundred** is an English franchise cricket tournament launched in 2021, built around a shortened 100-ball-per-innings format designed to be faster and more accessible than traditional Twenty20. Eight men's and eight women's teams, mostly named after England's historic Test grounds and cities, compete each August. The top team in each table qualifies straight for the final; the second- and third-placed teams play an Eliminator for the second final spot — the format that decided both of Sunday's finalists.

cards.title: Bumrah's shock Sri Lanka Test withdrawal sparks an internal BCCI blame game, reports say
cards.what_happened: Fresh reporting says the sudden nature of Bumrah's withdrawal wasn't a simple case of a player failing a late fitness test — it has instead triggered an **internal BCCI storm** over who knew what and when. According to the reports, the **CoE's sports science team had indicated to Agarkar and the selectors that Bumrah would be fit enough to travel** for the series, only for a subsequent, more thorough medical assessment to reveal his knee injury required a **longer recovery period** than first thought, forcing his withdrawal after all. That gap between the CoE's initial read and the final medical picture has reportedly left the chief selector's panel unhappy with how the CoE handled and communicated Bumrah's case. Compounding the issue, the report notes the **CoE has been without a full-time head of sports science** since Nitin Patel departed the role — a structural gap that may have contributed to the mixed signals. The BCCI is now said to be reviewing its **injury-management and communication protocols**. J&K's uncapped **Auqib Nabi**, who took 104 wickets across the last two Ranji Trophy seasons, remains in as Bumrah's replacement.

India closed play at **273/2** after choosing to bat first at Galle.
Padikkal and **KL Rahul** put on a **150-run partnership** before Rahul retired hurt on 77.
Captain **Shubman Gill** was the only big wicket to fall, out for 16 to Prabath Jayasuriya.
**Rishabh Pant** was unbeaten on 18 at the close alongside Padikkal.

depth.background: This is India's 600th Test match — a milestone only one other team (England) had reached before, and the first for any Asian side. India opted to bowl first when they won the toss (as covered earlier), leaving uncapped fast bowler Auqib Nabi out of the XI, with Jasprit Bumrah already ruled out of the series through injury. Devdutt Padikkal, a 24-year-old left-hander with a strong domestic first-class record, had played Tests before without converting a start into a century — making today's knock his first three-figure score at this level.

cards.title: Josh Hazlewood becomes just the ninth Australian to reach 300 Test wickets
cards.what_happened: During Australia's first Test against Bangladesh in Darwin, **Josh Hazlewood took a six-wicket haul**, dismissing Mominul Haque, Najmul Shanto, Mehidy Hasan Miraz, Hasan Mahmud, Taijul Islam and Ebadot Hossain, which carried him past **300 Test wickets** for his career. He becomes the **ninth Australian** to reach the milestone, and joins **Nathan Lyon, Pat Cummins and Mitchell Starc** as the fourth member of Australia's current attack to do so — the first time in Test history that four bowlers from the same attack have all individually passed 300 wickets while playing together. His career bowling average of **24.02** ranks behind only Glenn McGrath, Pat Cummins and Dennis Lillee among Australians with 300-plus Test wickets.
key_points: Hazlewood took **six wickets** in an innings against Bangladesh in Darwin to pass the milestone.
He's only the **ninth Australian bowler ever** to reach 300 Test wickets.
He joins **Nathan Lyon, Pat Cummins and Mitchell Starc** as teammates who've all crossed 300 — a first in Test history.
His bowling average of **24.02** is bettered by only **Glenn McGrath, Pat Cummins and Dennis Lillee** among Australians with 300+ wickets.

depth.background: Reaching 300 Test wickets is one of cricket's most respected milestones, achieved by only a small group of the format's greatest bowlers. Josh Hazlewood has been a mainstay of Australia's pace attack since debuting in 2014, prized for his metronomic accuracy alongside more express bowlers like Mitchell Starc and Pat Cummins. Australia's four-man pace-and-spin attack of Hazlewood, Starc, Cummins and off-spinner Nathan Lyon has been settled for years, making this milestone a landmark for the whole unit, not just Hazlewood individually.

cards.title: Bangladesh closes in on a stunning Test win as Australia slump to 161 for 4 following on in Darwin
cards.what_happened: Bangladesh posted a commanding first-innings total of **426**, built through the middle order, while paceman **Josh Hazlewood** was Australia's standout bowler with figures of **6 for 89**. In reply, Australia collapsed to just **198 all out**, handing Bangladesh a **228-run lead** and forcing Australia to follow on and bat again immediately. Batting a second time, Australia lost **Steven Smith**, one of the world's best Test batters, caught off spinner **Mehidy Hasan Miraz**, and closed the third day's play on **161 for 4**, with **Cameron Green (43 not out)** and **Alex Carey (19 not out)** still at the crease — still trailing Bangladesh's first-innings total by **67 runs**.
key_points: Bangladesh posted **426** in their first innings, a **228-run lead**, powered by **Josh Hazlewood's 6-89**
Australia were bowled out for just **198** in reply, forcing them to bat again
Australia closed Day 3 at **161 for 4**, still trailing by **67 runs**
Star batter **Steven Smith** was dismissed, caught off spinner **Mehidy Hasan Miraz**

depth.background: Bangladesh have never won a Test match in Australia, and Australia are one of the most dominant home Test sides in the sport — so any contest that puts Australia under real pressure on their own soil is unusual. This is the first Test of a two-match series in Darwin, played on a pitch that has clearly favored batting more than expected, with Bangladesh's middle order cashing in heavily in the first innings.

cards.title: Yashasvi Jaiswal run out in bizarre mid-pitch collision with Sri Lanka's bowler on Galle Test's opening day
cards.what_happened: Facing a delivery from Sri Lankan left-arm spinner **Keshara Nuwantha**, KL Rahul pushed the ball towards mid-on and immediately called for a single. As Jaiswal set off from the non-striker's end, Nuwantha — who had followed through and dived sharply to his right trying to stop the ball — collided with him, knocking him off balance. The contact left Jaiswal briefly stranded and disoriented, and by the time he recovered his footing, the fielding side had already gathered the ball and broken the stumps at the bowler's end with both batters caught out of their ground. Television replays showed the incident was accidental rather than deliberate obstruction by either side, and the third umpire confirmed the run-out. Jaiswal walked off for **32**, ending a promising start, while Rahul and the incoming Devdutt Padikkal steadied India to 101 for 1 at the lunch break.
key_points: Jaiswal was run out for **32** after colliding mid-pitch with Sri Lankan spinner **Keshara Nuwantha**, who had dived to stop the ball.
The mix-up started when **KL Rahul** tapped the ball to mid-on and set off for what looked like a routine single.
It is at least the **third time in his Test career** Jaiswal has lost his wicket to a running mix-up with a partner.
India recovered to **101/1 at lunch** on day one, with Rahul (32*) and **Devdutt Padikkal** (35*) rebuilding steadily.
The dismissal came on the opening day of India's historic **600th Test**, the first of a two-match series in Galle.

depth.background: India began their tour of Sri Lanka today by playing their **600th Test match** — only the third team in history, after England and Australia, to reach that mark. Yashasvi Jaiswal has been India's first-choice Test opener for the past two years and walked out with KL Rahul to start the innings after India won the toss and chose to bat. In cricket, the **non-striker** (the batter waiting at the bowler's end) must judge, in a split second, whether to run when their partner hits the ball — a call that occasionally goes wrong, sometimes with unusual consequences. Jaiswal himself has been part of more than one such mix-up earlier in his career.

cards.title: India win the toss and bat first in their historic 600th Test, but leave uncapped Auqib Nabi out of the XI at Galle
cards.what_happened: Play began on schedule at **Galle International Stadium**, with India winning the toss and opting to bat first on what looked, in Gill's own assessment, like a good batting surface. The announced XI answered yesterday's open question: **Auqib Nabi did not get his debut**. Instead, India fielded three specialist spinners — Ravindra Jadeja, **Kuldeep Yadav**, and uncapped spinner Manav Suthar — alongside pacers Mohammed Siraj and Prasidh Krishna, betting on spin-friendly Galle conditions over an extra seamer. The top order got off to a rocky start when **Yashasvi Jaiswal was run out** within the first hour, before KL Rahul and Devdutt Padikkal steadied the innings; India were past 70 runs for one wicket as the morning session progressed. This is officially India's 600th Test and their first match of the new World Test Championship cycle, played under Gill's captaincy on a day that also happens to be India's Independence Day.
key_points: India **won the toss and chose to bat first** in what is officially their **600th Test match**, only the third team ever to reach that number.
Uncapped pacer **Auqib Nabi was left out of the XI** despite his shock call-up, with India instead picking **three spinners** — Ravindra Jadeja, Kuldeep Yadav and Manav Suthar.
Opener **Yashasvi Jaiswal was run out** inside the first hour, an early setback for the new-look batting order.
The Test is India's **first fixture of the 2025–2027 World Test Championship cycle** and the first under new full-time captain **Shubman Gill**.
August 15 is **India's Independence Day**, adding symbolic weight to a match already billed as a milestone occasion.

thread.previously: Yesterday's story previewed India's 600th Test — a milestone only England and Australia had previously reached — with Shubman Gill captaining and uncapped seamer Auqib Nabi in the squad after Jasprit Bumrah was ruled out injured; the open question was whether Nabi would get a shock debut.
thread.changed: The match has now actually started: India won the toss and chose to bat, and the announced XI leaves Auqib Nabi out — India went in with Kuldeep Yadav and Manav Suthar as spinners alongside Jadeja instead of handing Nabi his debut. Play is underway, with India past 70 for the loss of Yashasvi Jaiswal, who was run out early.

depth.background: This is the same landmark Test previewed a day earlier: India entering their 600th match, a mark only England and Australia had reached before, at Galle's 50th-ever Test — a first for any Asian venue. Shubman Gill leads the side for the first time in a bilateral Test series since being installed as India's full-time red-ball captain, working alongside head coach **Gautam Gambhir**. Ahead of the game, India's pace attack had already lost **Jasprit Bumrah** to a knee injury, prompting the surprise squad inclusion of uncapped Jammu and Kashmir seamer Auqib Nabi — whose potential debut was the single biggest open question heading into the match.

cards.title: Cricket Ireland braces for protests as Afghanistan series ends at Stormont, with Amnesty warning against 'Taliban propaganda'
cards.what_happened: Ireland and Afghanistan play the **fifth and final ODI** of their series at **Stormont** today, August 15, with Afghanistan holding a strong lead after outplaying Ireland in earlier matches — including a 92-run win powered by **Ibrahim Zadran's 84**, while Ireland were bowled out for 207 despite fighting knocks from Cade Carmichael and Andy Balbirnie. Ahead of and during the series, **Amnesty International** publicly warned that hosting Afghanistan risked handing the **Taliban a propaganda platform**, and called on Cricket Ireland, its players, and the ICC to speak out on the treatment of Afghan women. Small protests, including demonstrators dressed in burkas, have already gathered outside the grounds during the earlier Stormont matches. **Cricket Ireland and the Police Service of Northern Ireland (PSNI)** say dedicated security and policing plans are in place to protect players, staff, and fans while also allowing lawful protest. Cricket Ireland had earlier admitted **'moral discomfort'** about the series but chose to proceed with it, arguing that engagement rather than isolation was the better path.
key_points: Ireland host Afghanistan for the **fifth and final match** of a five-game ODI series at **Stormont in Belfast** today.
**Amnesty International** has warned the fixtures risk being used as **'Taliban propaganda'** and urged Cricket Ireland and the ICC to speak out on Afghan women's rights.
Cricket Ireland says **security plans are in place**, with police confirming a **'proportionate policing plan'** for any demonstrations.
Small protests, including women in burkas, have already taken place outside grounds during earlier matches in the series.
**Afghanistan has dominated the series**, including a 92-run win built on Ibrahim Zadran's 84, leaving Ireland needing a big turnaround.

depth.background: Since the **Taliban retook power in Afghanistan in 2021**, women there have been banned from playing or even watching sport, barred from universities and parks, and — according to rights groups — hunted down if they try to keep playing in secret; many of Afghanistan's former women cricketers fled the country. Under ICC rules a men's team can keep its full-member status as long as it has a men's program, so **Afghanistan's men's team keeps playing internationally** even though its women's team has been effectively erased. That contradiction has made every Afghanistan men's fixture a flashpoint: **Australia and England have both cancelled or avoided bilateral series** against Afghanistan since 2021, while others, including Ireland, have gone ahead. This five-match ODI series began in Bready on the Irish mainland before shifting to Stormont in Belfast for its last three games.

cards.title: Bangladesh push Australia to the brink on day three in Darwin as the lead balloons past 200
cards.what_happened: Bangladesh resumed day three of the first Test in **Darwin** in a commanding position after posting **351 for 6** on day two, powered by **Tanzid Hasan's maiden Test century (101 runs)**, an **84 from captain Najmul Hossain Shanto**, a composed 49 from Mominul Haque, and Mehidy Hasan Miraz unbeaten on 32. That total gave Bangladesh a first-innings lead of **153 runs** over Australia's **198 all out**. As Australia batted again in their second innings on day three, the deficit kept growing — by the second session, Australia trailed by **216 runs**, with Marnus Labuschagne and Travis Head at the crease trying to build a partnership and avoid an innings defeat. Josh Hazlewood had taken 2 wickets for Australia's bowling attack the previous day but couldn't stop Bangladesh's lower order from extending the total.
key_points: By session two of **day three**, Australia trailed by **216 runs** in the first Test at Darwin — a huge deficit with the match past its halfway point.
Bangladesh's day two total of **351 for 6** was built on **Tanzid Hasan's maiden Test century (101)** and a gritty **84 from captain Najmul Hossain Shanto**.
Australia's first innings closed at just **198**, meaning Bangladesh's lead was already **153** before day three even started.
Marnus Labuschagne and Travis Head were at the crease trying to steady Australia's second innings as the gap widened further.
This is Bangladesh's **first tour of Australia in years**, and a win — or even a draw — from this position would be one of their **biggest overseas results ever**.

depth.background: Bangladesh have historically struggled on **fast, bouncy Australian pitches**, and playing in **Darwin** — an unusual, tropical Test venue for Australia — adds heat and humidity as extra variables. A five-day **Test match** is decided over four innings (two per side); building a big first-innings lead, as Bangladesh have done here, puts huge pressure on the team batting last because they're chasing a target on a worn pitch. **Marnus Labuschagne** and **Travis Head** are senior, experienced Australian batters whose job on day three was to prevent the deficit from Bangladesh's dominant batting from spiraling further out of control.

cards.title: Manchester Super Giants blitz SunRisers Leeds to reach the Hundred men's final at Lord's
cards.what_happened: Batting first under lights at the Oval, Manchester Super Giants were given a flying platform by Paul Walter and Heinrich Klaasen, who put on 114 runs together — Walter's innings included eight sixes, a new individual record for the franchise, as the pair took the total to 186 for 4 from their 100 balls. In reply, SunRisers Leeds never quite got the asking rate under control: Josh Tongue struck twice inside his opening spell, top-edging Mitch Marsh and trapping captain Zak Crawley leg-before four balls later, and despite a fighting effort from Harry Brook (49) and an unbeaten 54 from Ryan Rickelton, Leeds fell 20 runs short. The result ends SunRisers Leeds' 2026 campaign — hours after their women's side also lost their own Eliminator on the same night at the Oval — and sends Manchester Super Giants through to face Trent Rockets in Sunday's men's final at Lord's.
key_points: **Manchester Super Giants** beat **SunRisers Leeds** by **20 runs** in Friday night's Eliminator at the Kia Oval to book a spot in Sunday's men's final.

Opener **Paul Walter** smashed **80 off 46 balls** including a club-record **8 sixes** in an innings, sharing a **114-run third-wicket stand** with **Heinrich Klaasen (63 off 26)** — Manchester's biggest-ever third-wicket partnership in T20 cricket.
Manchester posted **186-4** from their 100 balls; SunRisers fell short despite fifties from **Harry Brook (49 off 31)** and **Ryan Rickelton (54 not out off 34)**.
Seamer **Josh Tongue** took **4 wickets for 26 runs**, removing SunRisers openers Mitch Marsh and captain Zak Crawley early to swing the chase back Manchester's way.
Manchester Super Giants now face **Trent Rockets** in the men's final at **Lord's on Sunday, August 16**, with SunRisers Leeds' 2026 campaign over.

depth.background: The Hundred is England's franchise short-form competition, where each innings is a fixed 100 balls rather than the usual 120 of T20 cricket, and the top four men's and women's teams from the group stage progress to knockout play. SunRisers Leeds had topped the group table and looked the form side coming into the knockouts, while Manchester Super Giants scraped into the playoffs on net run rate. Trent Rockets had already secured their place in the final by finishing group-stage leaders and winning their own semi-final-equivalent fixture, leaving the Oval Eliminator to decide their opponent.
